sentences.zh: 【唐紀八十一】　起閼逢困敦五月，盡柔兆攝提格，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 81] From the fifth month of Yanfeng Kundun through Rouzhao Shetige; a little more than two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 81] From the fifth month of Yanfeng Kundun through Rouzhao Shetige—spanning a little more than two years in all.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝下之下天祐元年（

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial—Lower Part, Lower Section: First Year of Tianyou (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial—Lower Part, Lower Section: First Year of Tianyou (

sentences.zh: 甲子，公元九零四年）

translations.literal: jiazi, 904 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiazi, 904 CE)

sentences.zh: 五月，丙寅，加河陽節度使張漢瑜同平章事。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on bingyin, Zhang Hanyu, military governor of Heyang, was made an Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingyin, Zhang Hanyu, military governor of Heyang, was appointed Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 帝宴朱全忠及百官於崇勳殿，既罷，復召全忠宴於內殿。

translations.literal: The emperor feasted Zhu Quanzhong and the officials in the Hall of Honored Merit; when it ended, he again summoned Quanzhong to feast in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held a banquet for Zhu Quanzhong and the officials in the Hall of Honored Merit; when it ended, he summoned Quanzhong again to feast in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 全忠疑，不入。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was suspicious and did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong grew suspicious and refused to enter.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「全忠不欲來，可令敬翔來。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If Quanzhong does not wish to come, you may have Jing Xiang come."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If Quanzhong does not wish to come, send Jing Xiang instead."

sentences.zh: 」全忠擿翔使去，曰：「翔亦醉矣。

translations.literal: " Quanzhong pushed Xiang to go away and said: "Xiang is drunk as well."
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong pushed Xiang away and said, "Xiang is drunk too."

sentences.zh: 」辛未，全忠東還，乙亥，至大梁。

translations.literal: " On xinwei, Quanzhong returned east; on yihai, he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: " On xinwei, Quanzhong returned east; on yihai, he reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 忠義節度使趙匡凝遣水軍上峽攻王建夔州，知渝州王宗阮等擊敗之。

translations.literal: Zhao Kuangning, military governor of Zhongyi, sent a naval force up the gorges to attack Wang Jian's Kuizhou; Wang Zongruan, prefect of Yuzhou, and others defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Kuangning, military governor of Zhongyi, sent a naval force up the Yangtze gorges to attack Wang Jian's Kuizhou, but Wang Zongruan, prefect of Yuzhou, and others defeated them.

sentences.zh: 萬州刺史張武作鐵絲亙絕江中流，立柵於兩端，謂之「鎖峽」。

translations.literal: Zhang Wu, prefect of Wanzhou, stretched iron cables across midstream, set palisades at both ends, and called it "Locking the Gorge."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wu, prefect of Wanzhou, stretched iron cables across the river midstream, erected palisades at both ends, and called the barrier "Locking the Gorge."

sentences.zh: 六月，李茂貞、王建、李繼徽傳檄合兵以討朱全忠。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Li Maozhen, Wang Jian, and Li Jihui circulated a proclamation and united their armies to campaign against Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Li Maozhen, Wang Jian, and Li Jihui issued a joint proclamation and combined their forces to campaign against Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 全忠以鎮國節度使朱友裕為行營都統，將步騎數萬擊之；

translations.literal: Quanzhong appointed Zhu Youyu, military governor of Zhenguo, commander-in-chief of the field camp, and led several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to strike them;
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong appointed Zhu Youyu, military governor of Zhenguo, commander-in-chief of the field camp, and led tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry against them;

sentences.zh: 命保大節度使劉鄩棄鄜州，引兵屯同州。

translations.literal: he ordered Liu Yun, military governor of Baoda, to abandon Binzhou and lead troops to encamp at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered Liu Yun, military governor of Baoda, to abandon Binzhou and station his troops at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，全忠引兵自大梁西討茂貞等。

translations.literal: On guichou, Quanzhong led troops from Daliang west to campaign against Maozhen and the others.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Quanzhong marched west from Daliang to campaign against Maozhen and his allies.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，甲子，過東都入見。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiazi, he passed through the Eastern Capital and entered to have an audience.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on jiazi, he passed through the Eastern Capital and had an audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 壬申，至河中。

translations.literal: On renshen, he reached Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, he reached Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 西川諸將勸王建乘李茂貞之衰，攻取鳳翔。

translations.literal: The generals of Xichuan urged Wang Jian to seize the moment of Li Maozhen's decline and attack and take Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian's generals in Xichuan urged him to strike while Li Maozhen was weak and seize Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 建以問節度判官馮涓，涓曰：「兵者凶器，殘民耗財，不可窮也。

translations.literal: Jian asked his military-governor's aide Feng Juan; Juan said: "Arms are an inauspicious instrument—they harm the people and drain wealth and must not be pursued to the limit."
translations.idiomatic: Jian consulted his military-governor's aide Feng Juan, who said, "War is an instrument of ill omen—it harms the people and drains the treasury, and must not be pursued without limit."

sentences.zh: 今梁、晉虎爭，勢不兩立，若並而為一，舉兵向蜀，雖諸葛亮復生，不能敵矣。

translations.literal: Now Liang and Jin contend like tigers, and their forces cannot coexist; if they unite as one and raise troops against Shu, even if Zhuge Liang were reborn, he could not withstand them.
translations.idiomatic: Liang and Jin are locked in a tiger's fight from which neither can back down; if they unite and march on Shu, not even a reborn Zhuge Liang could hold them off.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔，蜀之籓蔽，不若與之和親，結為婚姻，無事則務農訓兵，保固疆場，有事則覘其機事，觀釁而動，可以萬全。

translations.literal: Fengxiang is Shu's screen and shield; better to seek harmony and kinship with them and seal a marriage alliance—when there is peace, devote yourself to farming and training troops and securing the borders; when trouble arises, watch their opportunities and move when you see an opening, and you may be wholly secure.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang is Shu's shield on the frontier; you would do better to seek peace and a marriage alliance—cultivate the fields and train your troops in quiet times, hold your borders firm, and in crisis watch their moves and strike only when you see an opening. That is the path to complete security.

sentences.zh: 」建曰：「善！

translations.literal: " Jian said: "Excellent!"
translations.idiomatic: " Jian said, "Excellent!"

sentences.zh: 茂貞雖庸才，然有強悍之名，遠近畏之，與全忠力爭則不足，自守則有餘，使為吾籓蔽，所利多矣。

translations.literal: Maozhen may be a mediocre talent, yet he bears a name for fierceness and men near and far fear him; he is not equal to contending with Quanzhong by force, but more than sufficient to hold his own—to make him our screen brings many advantages.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen is no great genius, but his reputation for fierceness makes men far and near fear him; he cannot match Quanzhong in open struggle, yet he can hold his own—and as our shield on the frontier, the gain is great.

sentences.zh: 」乃與茂貞修好。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he restored friendly relations with Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: " He then restored friendly relations with Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 丙子，茂貞遣判官趙鍠如西川，為其侄天雄節度使繼崇求婚，建以女妻之。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Maozhen sent his aide Zhao Heng to Xichuan to seek a marriage on behalf of his nephew Jichong, military governor of Tianxiong; Jian gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Maozhen sent his aide Zhao Heng to Xichuan to seek a bride for his nephew Jichong, military governor of Tianxiong; Wang Jian gave him a daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 茂貞數求貨及甲兵於建，建皆與之。

translations.literal: Maozhen repeatedly asked Jian for goods and armor and weapons; Jian gave him all he requested.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen repeatedly asked Wang Jian for goods, armor, and weapons, and Jian supplied everything he requested.

sentences.zh: 王建賦斂重，人莫敢言。

translations.literal: Wang Jian's levies were heavy, and no one dared speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian's taxes and levies were crushing, yet no one dared complain.

sentences.zh: 馮涓因建生日獻頌，先美功德，後言生民之苦。

translations.literal: On Jian's birthday Feng Juan presented a eulogy that first praised his merit and virtue, then spoke of the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: On Wang Jian's birthday, Feng Juan presented a eulogy that first praised his achievements, then spoke of the people's suffering.

sentences.zh: 建愧謝曰：「如君忠諫，功業何憂！

translations.literal: Jian, ashamed, thanked him and said: "With loyal remonstrance such as yours, what need I fear for my enterprise!"
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Jian thanked him and said, "With counsel as loyal as yours, what need I fear for my enterprise!"

sentences.zh: 」賜之金帛。

translations.literal: " He rewarded him with gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: " He rewarded him with gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 自是賦斂稍損。

translations.literal: From this time the levies were somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: After that, the levies were somewhat eased.

sentences.zh: 初，朱全忠自鳳翔迎車駕還，見德王裕眉目疏秀，且年齒已壯，惡之，私謂崔胤曰：「德王嘗奸帝位，豈可復留！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhu Quanzhong escorted the imperial carriage back from Fengxiang, he saw that Prince De, Yu, had fine, open features and was already grown in years; he hated this and said privately to Cui Yin: "Prince De once coveted the throne—how can he be allowed to remain!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhu Quanzhong escorted the emperor back from Fengxiang, he saw that Prince De, Li Yu, had handsome, refined features and was already a grown man; he took alarm and said privately to Cui Yin, "Prince De once coveted the throne—how can he be allowed to remain!"

sentences.zh: 公何不言之！

translations.literal: Why do you not speak of it!"
translations.idiomatic: Why do you not speak of it to the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 」胤言於帝。

translations.literal: " Yin spoke to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin relayed this to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝問全忠，全忠曰：「陛下父子之間，臣安敢竊議，此崔胤賣臣耳。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Quanzhong; Quanzhong said: "Between Your Majesty and your son, how dare your servant presume to comment in private—this is Cui Yin selling out your servant."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Quanzhong, who replied, "Between Your Majesty and your son, how dare I presume to comment in private? This is Cui Yin betraying me to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」帝自離長安，日憂不測，與皇后終日沉飲，或相對涕泣。

translations.literal: " Since leaving Chang'an, the emperor daily feared the unforeseen; with the empress he drank deep all day, or they wept face to face.
translations.idiomatic: " Since leaving Chang'an, the emperor lived in daily dread of what might befall him; he and the empress drowned their days in drink, or sat facing each other in tears.

sentences.zh: 全忠使樞密使蔣玄暉伺察帝，動靜皆知之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong had the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Jiang Xuanhui spy on the emperor; his every movement was known.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong had Jiang Xuanhui, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, spy on the emperor, so that his every move was reported.

sentences.zh: 帝從容謂玄暉曰：「德王，朕之愛子，全忠何故堅欲殺之？

translations.literal: At ease, the emperor said to Xuanhui: "Prince De is my beloved son—why does Quanzhong insist on killing him?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said calmly to Xuanhui, "Prince De is my beloved son—why does Quanzhong insist on having him killed?"

sentences.zh: 」因泣下，嚙中指血流。

translations.literal: " He wept, and bit his middle finger until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: " He wept, biting his middle finger until blood ran.

sentences.zh: 玄暉具以語全忠，全忠愈不自安。

translations.literal: Xuanhui reported all this to Quanzhong, and Quanzhong grew still more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui reported everything to Quanzhong, who grew still more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 時李茂貞、楊崇本、李克用、劉仁恭、王建、楊行密、趙匡凝移檄往來，皆以興復為辭。

translations.literal: At this time Li Maozhen, Yang Chongben, Li Keyong, Liu Rengong, Wang Jian, Yang Xingmi, and Zhao Kuangning exchanged proclamations back and forth, all taking restoration as their plea.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Maozhen, Yang Chongben, Li Keyong, Liu Rengong, Wang Jian, Yang Xingmi, and Zhao Kuangning exchanged proclamations among themselves, all invoking the restoration of the Tang.

sentences.zh: 全忠方引兵討，以帝有英氣，恐變生於中，欲立幼君，易謀禪代。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was just then leading troops on campaign; because the emperor had a spirited bearing, he feared trouble arising within and wished to set up a young ruler, making it easier to plot abdication and usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was campaigning at the time; the emperor's spirited bearing alarmed him, and he feared trouble from within the palace. He wished to install a young ruler, making abdication and usurpation easier to arrange.

sentences.zh: 乃遣判官李振至洛陽，與玄暉及左龍武統軍朱友恭、右龍武統軍氏叔琮等圖之。

translations.literal: He then sent his aide Li Zhen to Luoyang to plot it with Xuanhui, Zhu Yougong, commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army, Shi Shuzong, commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his aide Li Zhen to Luoyang to plot with Xuanhui, Zhu Yougong of the Left Dragon Martial Army, Shi Shuzong of the Right Dragon Martial Army, and others.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，帝在椒殿，玄暉選龍武牙官史太等百人夜叩宮門，言軍前有急奏，欲面見帝。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on renyin, the emperor was in the Jiao Hall; Xuanhui selected a hundred Dragon Martial junior officers led by Shi Tai and at night knocked on the palace gate, saying there was urgent memorial business at the front and they wished an audience with the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renyin, the emperor was in the Jiao Hall. Xuanhui selected a hundred Dragon Martial junior officers led by Shi Tai, who knocked on the palace gate at night claiming urgent military dispatches and demanding an audience.

sentences.zh: 夫人裴貞一開門見兵，曰：「急奏何以兵為？

translations.literal: Lady Pei Zhenyi opened the gate, saw troops, and said: "Why bring soldiers for an urgent memorial?"
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pei Zhenyi opened the gate, saw armed men, and said, "Why bring soldiers for an urgent memorial?"

sentences.zh: 」史太殺之。

translations.literal: " Shi Tai killed her.
translations.idiomatic: " Shi Tai killed her.

sentences.zh: 玄暉問：「至尊安在？

translations.literal: Xuanhui asked: "Where is His Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui called out, "Where is His Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 」昭儀李漸榮臨軒呼曰：「寧殺我曹，勿傷大家！

translations.literal: " Lady of Bright Deportment Li Jianrong leaned from the balustrade and cried: "Better kill us than harm His Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: " Lady of Bright Deportment Li Jianrong leaned from the balustrade and cried, "Kill us if you must, but spare His Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 」帝方醉，遽起，單衣繞柱走，史太追而弒之。

translations.literal: " The emperor, who was drunk, sprang up in his undergarments, ran around a pillar, and Shi Tai pursued and assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, who was drunk, sprang up in his undergarments and fled around a pillar; Shi Tai pursued and killed him.

sentences.zh: 漸榮以身蔽帝，太亦殺之。

translations.literal: Jianrong shielded the emperor with her body; Tai killed her as well.
translations.idiomatic: Jianrong shielded the emperor with her body, and Tai killed her too.

sentences.zh: 又欲殺何-{后}-，-{后}-求哀於玄暉，乃釋之。

translations.literal: They also wished to kill Empress He; the empress begged Xuanhui for mercy, and he released her.
translations.idiomatic: They also meant to kill Empress He; she begged Xuanhui for mercy, and he spared her.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，蔣玄暉矯詔稱李漸榮、裴貞一弒逆，宜立輝王祚為皇太子，更名柷，監軍國事。

translations.literal: On guimao, Jiang Xuanhui forged an edict stating that Li Jianrong and Pei Zhenyi had committed regicide, and that Prince Hui, Zuo, should be made crown prince, renamed Zhu, and put in charge of state and military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Jiang Xuanhui forged an edict declaring that Li Jianrong and Pei Zhenyi had murdered the emperor, and that Prince Hui, Li Zuo, should be made crown prince, renamed Zhu, and placed in charge of state and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 又矯皇后令，太子於柩前即位。

translations.literal: He also forged an order from the empress that the crown prince should ascend the throne before the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: He also forged an order from the empress commanding the crown prince to ascend the throne before the coffin.

sentences.zh: 宮中恐懼，不敢出聲哭。

translations.literal: Within the palace all were terrified and dared not weep aloud.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace everyone was terrified and dared not weep aloud.

sentences.zh: 丙午，昭宣帝即位，時年十三。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Emperor Zhaoxuan ascended the throne; he was then thirteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Emperor Zhaoxuan ascended the throne at the age of thirteen.

sentences.zh: 李克用復以張承業為監軍。

translations.literal: Li Keyong again appointed Zhang Chengye military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong again appointed Zhang Chengye as his military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 淮南將李神福攻鄂州未下，會疾病，還廣陵，楊行密以舒州團練使泌陽劉存代為招討使。

translations.literal: The Huainan general Li Shenfu attacked Ezhou but could not take it; he fell ill, returned to Guangling, and Yang Xingmi replaced him as commander for the campaign with Liu Cun of Biyang, regimental commander of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan general Li Shenfu besieged Ezhou without success, then fell ill and returned to Guangling; Yang Xingmi replaced him with Liu Cun of Biyang, regimental commander of Shuzhou, as commander for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 神福尋卒。

translations.literal: Shenfu soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu soon died.

sentences.zh: 宣州觀察使台濛卒，楊行密以其子牙內諸軍使渥為宣州觀察使，右牙都指揮使徐溫謂渥曰：「王寢疾而嫡嗣出籓，此必奸臣之謀。

translations.literal: Tai Meng, governor of Xuanzhou, died; Yang Xingmi made his son Wo, commissioner of the Palace Inner Guards, governor of Xuanzhou; Xu Wen, right commander of the Palace Guards, said to Wo: "The prince is gravely ill while the legitimate heir is sent out to a province—this must be a treacherous minister's plot."
translations.idiomatic: Tai Meng, governor of Xuanzhou, died. Yang Xingmi appointed his son Wo, commissioner of the Palace Inner Guards, governor of Xuanzhou. Xu Wen, right commander of the Palace Guards, told Wo, "The prince is gravely ill while the legitimate heir is sent to a distant province—this must be a treacherous minister's plot."

sentences.zh: 他日相召，非溫使者及王令書，慎無亟來！

translations.literal: If you are summoned hereafter, unless the messenger is from Wen or the order bears the prince's seal, be careful not to come in haste!"
translations.idiomatic: If you are summoned later, unless the messenger is mine or the order bears the prince's seal, do not come in haste!"

sentences.zh: 」渥泣謝而行。

translations.literal: " Wo wept, thanked him, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Wo wept, thanked him, and set out.

sentences.zh: 九月，己巳，尊皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on jisi, the empress was honored as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jisi, the empress was honored as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠引兵北屯永壽，南至駱谷，鳳翔、邠寧兵竟不出。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong led troops north to encamp at Yongshou and south to Luogu, but the Fengxiang and Binning forces never came out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong led troops north to Yongshou and south to Luogu, but the Fengxiang and Binning armies never came out to fight.

sentences.zh: 辛未，東還。

translations.literal: On xinwei, he returned east.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, he returned east.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，辛卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the xinmao new moon, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the xinmao new moon, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠聞朱友恭等弒昭宗，陽驚，號哭自投於地，曰：「奴輩負我，令我受惡名於萬代！

translations.literal: When Zhu Quanzhong heard that Zhu Yougong and the others had assassinated Emperor Zhaozong, he feigned shock, wailed, and threw himself to the ground, saying: "Those slaves have betrayed me and made me bear an evil name for ten thousand generations!"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong learned that Zhu Yougong and the others had murdered Emperor Zhaozong, he feigned shock, wailed, and threw himself to the ground, crying, "Those slaves have betrayed me and left me with an evil name for all eternity!"

sentences.zh: 」癸巳，至東都，伏梓宮慟哭流悌，又見帝，自陳非己志，請討賊。

translations.literal: " On guisi, he reached the Eastern Capital, prostrated himself before the coffin, and wept until tears streamed; he also saw the emperor, declared it was not his intent, and asked to campaign against the criminals.
translations.idiomatic: " On guisi, he reached the Eastern Capital, prostrated himself before the coffin, and wept until tears streamed down his face; he also saw the emperor, declared that the murder was not his doing, and asked permission to hunt down the criminals.

sentences.zh: 先是，護駕軍士有掠米於市者，甲午，全忠奏朱友恭、氏叔琮不戢士卒，侵擾市肆，友恭貶崖州司戶，複姓名李彥威，叔琮貶白州司戶，尋皆賜自盡。

translations.literal: Earlier, escort troops had plundered grain in the market; on jiawu, Quanzhong memorialized that Zhu Yougong and Shi Shuzong had not restrained their soldiers and had harassed the marketplaces. Yougong was demoted to registrar of Yazhou and his original name Li Yanwei was restored; Shuzong was demoted to registrar of Baizhou; soon both were ordered to take their own lives.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, escort troops had plundered grain in the markets. On jiawu, Quanzhong reported that Zhu Yougong and Shi Shuzong had failed to restrain their men and had harassed the markets. Yougong was demoted to registrar of Yazhou and his original name, Li Yanwei, was restored; Shuzong was demoted to registrar of Baizhou; soon both were ordered to commit suicide.

sentences.zh: 彥威臨刑大呼曰：「賣我以塞天下之謗，如鬼神何！

translations.literal: At execution Yanwei shouted: "You sell me out to stifle the world's slander—what of the spirits and gods!"
translations.idiomatic: At the execution Yanwei shouted, "You sell me out to silence the world's blame—what will you say to heaven and earth!"

sentences.zh: 行事如此，望有後乎！

translations.literal: Conduct affairs thus—can you hope for posterity!"
translations.idiomatic: Act like this—do you expect to leave descendants!"

sentences.zh: 丙申，天平節度使，張全義來朝。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Zhang Quanyi, military governor of Tianping, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Zhang Quanyi, military governor of Tianping, came to court.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，復以全忠為宣武、護國、宣義、天平節度使，以全義為河南尹兼忠武節度使、判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Quanzhong was again made military governor of Xuanwu, Huguo, Xuanyi, and Tianping; Quanyi was made prefect of Henan and military governor of Zhongwu and given charge of the Six Armies and the palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Quanzhong was restored as military governor of Xuanwu, Huguo, Xuanyi, and Tianping; Quanyi was made prefect of Henan and military governor of Zhongwu, with charge of the Six Armies and palace guards.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，全忠辭赴鎮，良戌，至大梁。

translations.literal: On yisi, Quanzhong took leave to go to his command; on gengxu, he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Quanzhong took leave to return to his command; on gengxu, he reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 鎮國節度使朱友裕薨於梨園。

translations.literal: Zhu Youyu, military governor of Zhenguo, died at the Pear Garden camp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youyu, military governor of Zhenguo, died at the Pear Garden camp.

sentences.zh: 光州叛楊行密，降朱全忠，行密遣兵圍之，與鄂州皆告急於全忠。

translations.literal: Guangzhou rebelled against Yang Xingmi and surrendered to Zhu Quanzhong; Xingmi sent troops to besiege it, and both it and Ezhou sent urgent appeals to Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou rebelled against Yang Xingmi and surrendered to Zhu Quanzhong; Xingmi sent troops to besiege it, and both Guangzhou and Ezhou sent urgent appeals to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊辰，全忠自將兵五萬自穎州濟淮，軍於霍丘，分兵救鄂州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuchen, Quanzhong personally led fifty thousand troops from Yingzhou across the Huai, encamped at Huoqiu, and divided forces to relieve Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuchen, Quanzhong personally led fifty thousand troops from Yingzhou across the Huai, encamped at Huoqiu, and divided his forces to relieve Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 淮南兵釋光州之圍還廣陵，按兵不出戰，全忠分命諸將大掠淮南以困之。

translations.literal: The Huainan army lifted the siege of Guangzhou and returned to Guangling, held their troops and did not go out to battle; Quanzhong ordered his various generals to raid widely across Huainan to wear them down.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan forces lifted the siege of Guangzhou and returned to Guangling, holding their troops back from battle; Quanzhong ordered his generals to raid widely across Huainan to wear them down.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐潛遣衢州羅城使葉讓殺刺史陳璋，事洩。

translations.literal: Qian Liu secretly sent Ye Rang, commissioner of the outer wall of Quzhou, to kill the prefect Chen Zhang; the plot was exposed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu secretly sent Ye Rang, commissioner of Quzhou's outer wall, to assassinate Prefect Chen Zhang, but the plot was exposed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，璋斬讓而叛，降於楊行密。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Zhang executed Rang and rebelled, surrendering to Yang Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Chen Zhang executed Ye Rang, rebelled, and surrendered to Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 初，馬殷弟賨，性沉重，事孫儒，為百勝指揮使。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ma Yin's younger brother Cong was grave in temperament; he served Sun Ru as commander of the Hundred Victories Army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ma Yin's younger brother Cong was a man of grave temperament; he had served Sun Ru as commander of the Hundred Victories Army.

sentences.zh: 儒死，事楊行密，屢有功，遷黑雲指揮使。

translations.literal: When Ru died, he served Yang Xingmi, won repeated merit, and was promoted to commander of the Black Cloud Army.
translations.idiomatic: After Ru's death he entered Yang Xingmi's service, won repeated distinction, and was promoted to commander of the Black Cloud Army.

sentences.zh: 行密嘗從容問其兄弟，乃知為殷之弟，大驚曰：「吾常怪汝器度瑰偉，果非常人，當遣汝歸。

translations.literal: Xingmi once asked him at ease about his brothers and learned he was Yin's younger brother; greatly startled, he said: "I have long marveled at your imposing bearing—you are indeed no ordinary man—and ought to send you home."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi once asked him casually about his family and learned he was Ma Yin's younger brother. Greatly startled, he said, "I have long marveled at your imposing bearing—you are no ordinary man—and I ought to send you home."

sentences.zh: 」賨泣辭曰：「賨西殘兵，大王不殺而寵任之，湖南地近，嘗得兄聲問，賨事大王久，不願歸也。

translations.literal: " Cong wept and declined, saying: "I was a remnant soldier of the Huai west; Your Highness did not kill me but favored and employed me. Hunan is near, and I have often had word from my brother, yet I have served Your Highness long and do not wish to return."
translations.idiomatic: " Cong wept and declined, saying, "I was a remnant soldier from the Huai west; you spared me and gave me your trust. Hunan is near, and I have often heard from my brother, yet I have served you long and do not wish to leave."

sentences.zh: 」行密固遣之。

translations.literal: " Xingmi insisted on sending him back.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingmi insisted on sending him home.

sentences.zh: 是歲，賨歸長沙，行密親餞之郊。

translations.literal: That year Cong returned to Changsha; Xingmi personally saw him off beyond the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: That year Cong returned to Changsha, and Xingmi personally saw him off beyond the city.

sentences.zh: 賨至長沙，殷表賨為節度副使。

translations.literal: When Cong reached Changsha, Yin memorialized to make him deputy military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong reached Changsha, Ma Yin memorialized to appoint him deputy military governor.

sentences.zh: 它日，殷議入貢天子，賨曰：「楊王地廣兵強，與吾鄰接，不若與之結好，大可以為緩急之授，小可通商旅之利。

translations.literal: Another day Yin discussed sending tribute to the Son of Heaven; Cong said: "The Prince of Yang holds broad territory and strong armies and borders us—better to seek friendship with him: in great matters he may be a source of aid in urgency, in small matters we may gain the profit of merchant traffic."
translations.idiomatic: On another day Ma Yin discussed sending tribute to the emperor. Cong said, "The Prince of Yang holds broad lands and a strong army and borders our realm—we would do better to seek his friendship. In great matters he could aid us in crisis; in small matters we could profit from trade."

sentences.zh: 」殷作色曰：「楊王不事天子，一旦朝廷致討，罪將及吾。

translations.literal: " Yin changed countenance and said: "The Prince of Yang does not serve the Son of Heaven—if the court should one day move to punish him, the guilt will reach us."
translations.idiomatic: " Ma Yin flushed with anger and said, "The Prince of Yang does not serve the emperor—if the court moves against him, we will be implicated."

sentences.zh: 汝置此論，勿為吾禍！

translations.literal: Put aside this talk and do not bring disaster upon me!"
translations.idiomatic: Put aside this talk—do not bring disaster upon me!"

sentences.zh: 初，清海節度使徐彥若遺表薦副使劉隱權留後，朝廷以兵部尚書崔遠為清海節度使。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xu Yanruo, military governor of Qinghai, left a memorial recommending his deputy Liu Yin as acting governor; the court appointed Cui Yuan, Minister of War, military governor of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu Yanruo, military governor of Qinghai, had left a memorial recommending his deputy Liu Yin as acting governor; the court appointed Cui Yuan, Minister of War, as military governor of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 遠至江陵，聞嶺南多盜，且畏隱不受代，不敢前，朝廷召遠還。

translations.literal: Yuan reached Jiangling, heard that bandits were numerous in Lingnan, and feared that Yin would not accept replacement; he dared not advance, and the court recalled Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan reached Jiangling, heard that bandits were rife in Lingnan, and feared that Liu Yin would refuse to yield his post; he dared not proceed, and the court recalled him.

sentences.zh: 隱遣使以重賂結朱全忠，乃奏以隱為清海節度使。

translations.literal: Yin sent envoys with heavy bribes to win over Zhu Quanzhong, who then memorialized to make Yin military governor of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent envoys with heavy bribes to win over Zhu Quanzhong, who then memorialized to appoint Yin military governor of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 昭宣光烈孝皇帝

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaoxuan, the Bright, Mighty, and Filial
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaoxuan, the Bright, Mighty, and Filial

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝下之下天祐二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial—Lower Part, Lower Section: Second Year of Tianyou (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial—Lower Part, Lower Section: Second Year of Tianyou (

sentences.zh: 乙丑，公元九零五年）

translations.literal: yichou, 905 CE)
translations.idiomatic: yichou, 905 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，朱全忠遣諸將進兵逼壽州。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Zhu Quanzhong sent his generals to advance troops and press Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Zhu Quanzhong sent his generals to advance on Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 潤州團練安仁義勇決得士心，故淮南將王茂章攻之，逾年不克。

translations.literal: An Renyi, regimental commander of Runzhou, was bold and resolute and won the soldiers' hearts; therefore the Huainan general Wang Maozhang attacked him for more than a year without taking the city.
translations.idiomatic: An Renyi, regimental commander of Runzhou, was bold and resolute and won his men's loyalty; the Huainan general Wang Maozhang besieged him for more than a year without success.

sentences.zh: 楊行密使謂之曰：「汝之功，吾不忘也，能束身自歸，當以汝為行軍副使，但不掌兵耳。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi's envoy said to him: "Your merit—I shall not forget it; if you can bind yourself and surrender of your own accord, I shall appoint you Deputy Field Commander, but you shall not command troops."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi's envoy told him, "I shall not forget what you have done. If you submit and surrender yourself, you will be made Deputy Field Commander—but you will not hold command of troops."

sentences.zh: 」仁義不從。

translations.literal: " Renyi refused.
translations.idiomatic: " Renyi refused.

sentences.zh: 茂章為地道入城，遂克之。

translations.literal: Maozhang dug a tunnel into the city and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang dug a tunnel into the city and captured it.

sentences.zh: 仁義舉族登樓，眾不敢逼。

translations.literal: Renyi led his entire clan up a tower; none dared press him.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi brought his whole family up onto a tower, and no one dared approach.

sentences.zh: 先是，攻城諸將見仁義輒罵之，惟李德誠不然，至是仁義召德誠登樓，謂曰：「汝有禮，吾今以為汝功。

translations.literal: Earlier, the generals besieging the city cursed Renyi whenever they saw him; only Li Decheng did not. Now Renyi summoned Decheng up the tower and said: "You have courtesy—I make this your achievement today."
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the besieging generals had cursed Renyi whenever they saw him, but Li Decheng alone had not. Now Renyi summoned Decheng to the tower and said, "You showed me courtesy—I count this as your accomplishment."

sentences.zh: 」且以愛妾贈之。

translations.literal: " He also gave him his favorite concubine as a gift.
translations.idiomatic: " He also presented his favorite concubine to him.

sentences.zh: 乃擲弓於地，德誠掖之而下，並其子斬於廣陵市。

translations.literal: He then threw his bow to the ground; Decheng supported him down, and both he and his son were beheaded in the Guangling market.
translations.idiomatic: He cast his bow to the ground. Decheng helped him down, and both he and his son were executed in the Guangling market.

sentences.zh: 兩浙兵圍陳詢於睦州，楊行密遣西南招討使陶雅將兵救之。

translations.literal: Two-Zhe troops besieged Chen Xun at Muzhou; Yang Xingmi sent the Southwest Campaign Commissioner Tao Ya with troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from the Two Zhe regions besieged Chen Xun at Muzhou. Yang Xingmi sent Tao Ya, Commissioner for the Southwest Campaign, with an army to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 軍中夜驚，士卒多逾壘亡去，左右及裨將韓球奔告之，雅安臥不應，須臾自定，亡者皆還。

translations.literal: The army was alarmed at night; many soldiers climbed over the ramparts and fled. Attendants and the deputy general Han Qiu rushed to report it; Ya lay in bed and did not respond. Shortly all calmed, and those who had fled all returned.
translations.idiomatic: The camp panicked at night, and many soldiers climbed over the walls and deserted. Attendants and the deputy general Han Qiu came running to report it, but Tao Ya lay in bed and made no reply. Before long the panic subsided on its own, and the deserters all came back.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐遣其從弟鎰及指揮使顧全武、王球御之，為雅所敗，虜鎰及球以歸。

translations.literal: Qian Liu sent his younger cousin Yi and the commanders Gu Quanwu and Wang Qiu to oppose them; they were defeated by Ya, who captured Yi and Qiu and brought them back.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent his younger cousin Yi and the commanders Gu Quanwu and Wang Qiu to meet them. Tao Ya defeated them and captured Yi and Wang Qiu, bringing them back as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 庚午，朱全忠命李振知青州事，代王師範。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Zhu Quanzhong ordered Li Zhen to oversee Qingzhou affairs, replacing Wang Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Zhu Quanzhong placed Li Zhen in charge of Qingzhou, replacing Wang Shifan.

sentences.zh: 全忠圍壽州，州人閉壁不出。

translations.literal: Quanzhong besieged Shouzhou; the people of the prefecture shut the walls and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong besieged Shouzhou, but the defenders barred the gates and refused to sally.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃自霍丘引歸，二月，辛卯，至大梁。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then withdrew from Huoqiu; in the second month, on xinmao, he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then withdrew from Huoqiu. In the second month, on xinmao, he arrived at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 李振至青州，王師範舉族西遷，至濮陽，素服乘驢而進。

translations.literal: When Li Zhen reached Qingzhou, Wang Shifan moved his entire clan west; reaching Puyang, he wore plain robes and rode a donkey as he went forward.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhen reached Qingzhou, Wang Shifan moved his whole family west. At Puyang he wore mourning dress and rode a donkey as he went.

sentences.zh: 至大梁，全忠客之。

translations.literal: Reaching Daliang, Quanzhong received him as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Daliang, Quanzhong treated him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 表李振為青州留後。

translations.literal: He memorialized to make Li Zhen acting governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to appoint Li Zhen acting governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以安南節度使、同平章事朱全昱為太師，致仕。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Zhu Quanyu, military governor of Annam and Associate Grand Councillor, was made Grand Preceptor and retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Zhu Quanyu, military governor of Annam and Associate Grand Councillor, was made Grand Preceptor and granted retirement.

sentences.zh: 全昱，全忠之兄也，戇樸無能，先領安南，全忠自請罷之。

translations.literal: Quanyu was Quanzhong's elder brother—dull, simple, and without ability. He had earlier held Annam; Quanzhong himself requested that he be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyu was Quanzhong's elder brother—simple-minded and incompetent. He had previously held Annam, and Quanzhong himself requested that the appointment be revoked.

sentences.zh: 是日社，全忠使蔣玄暉邀昭宗諸子：德王裕、棣王祤、虔王禊、沂王禋、遂王禕、景王祕、祁王祺、雅王禛、瓊王祥，置酒九曲池，酒酣，悉縊殺之，投屍池中。

translations.literal: That day was the She sacrifice; Quanzhong had Jiang Xuanhui invite Emperor Zhaozong's sons—Prince De, Yu; Prince Di, Qi; Prince Qian, Xi; Prince Yi, Yin; Prince Sui, Yi; Prince Jing, Mi; Prince Qi, Qi; Prince Ya, Zhen; and Prince Qiong, Xiang—set wine at the Nine-Bend Pool, and when they were deep in drink, strangled them all and threw their bodies into the pool.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of the She sacrifice, Quanzhong had Jiang Xuanhui invite Emperor Zhaozong's sons—Princes De (Yu), Di (Qi), Qian (Xi), Yi (Yin), Sui (Yi), Jing (Mi), Qi (Qi), Ya (Zhen), and Qiong (Xiang)—to a banquet at the Nine-Bend Pool. When they were drunk, he had them all strangled and their bodies thrown into the pool.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣其將曹延祚將兵與杜洪共守鄂州，庚子，淮南將劉存攻拔之，執洪、延祚及汴兵千餘人送廣陵，悉誅之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent his general Cao Yanzuo with troops to hold Ezhou together with Du Hong. On gengzi, the Huainan general Liu Cun attacked and took it, seized Hong, Yanzuo, and more than a thousand Bian troops, sent them to Guangling, and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent his general Cao Yanzuo with troops to defend Ezhou jointly with Du Hong. On gengzi, the Huainan general Liu Cun stormed and captured the city, seized Hong, Yanzuo, and more than a thousand Bian soldiers, sent them to Guangling, and had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 行密以存為鄂岳觀察使。

translations.literal: Xingmi made Cun Governor of E and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi appointed Liu Cun Governor of Ezhou and Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 己酉，葬聖穆景文孝皇帝於和陵，廟號昭宗。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial Emperor was buried at He Mausoleum; his temple name was Zhaozong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial Emperor was interred at He Mausoleum with the temple name Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 三月，庚午，以王師範為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month, on gengwu, Wang Shifan was made military governor of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on gengwu, Wang Shifan was appointed military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以門下侍郎、同平章事獨孤損同平章事，充靜海節度使；

translations.literal: On wuyin, Dugu Sun, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, was made Associate Grand Councillor and appointed military governor of Jinghai;
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Dugu Sun, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, was reappointed Associate Grand Councillor and sent out as military governor of Jinghai;

sentences.zh: 以禮部侍郎河間張文蔚同平章事。

translations.literal: Zhang Wenwei of Hejian, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, was made Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wenwei of Hejian, Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, was appointed Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以門下侍郎、同平章事裴樞為左僕射，崔遠為右僕射，並罷政事。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Pei Shu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Cui Yuan was made Right Vice Director; both were removed from state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Pei Shu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Cui Yuan Right Vice Director; both were dismissed from the chief counsel.

sentences.zh: 初，柳璨及第，不四年為宰相，性傾巧輕佻。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Can passed the examinations; in less than four years he became chancellor. By nature he was scheming, artful, and frivolous.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Can had passed the civil examinations and become chancellor in less than four years. By nature he was scheming, frivolous, and unserious.

sentences.zh: 時天子左右皆朱全忠腹心，璨曲意事之。

translations.literal: At the time those around the Son of Heaven were all Zhu Quanzhong's trusted men; Can bent himself to serve them with artifice.
translations.idiomatic: At the time those around the emperor were all Zhu Quanzhong's trusted agents, and Can went out of his way to curry favor with them.

sentences.zh: 同列裴樞、崔遠、獨孤損皆朝廷宿望，意輕之，璨以為憾。

translations.literal: His colleagues Pei Shu, Cui Yuan, and Dugu Sun were all longstanding pillars of the court; they looked down on him, and Can resented it.
translations.idiomatic: His colleagues Pei Shu, Cui Yuan, and Dugu Sun were all senior statesmen of long standing, and they looked down on him—a grievance Can nursed.

sentences.zh: 和王傅張廷范，本優人，有寵於全忠，奏以為太常卿。

translations.literal: The Prince of He's tutor Zhang Tingfan had originally been an entertainer and enjoyed Quanzhong's favor; a memorial was submitted to make him Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tingfan, tutor to the Prince of He, had originally been a performer and enjoyed Quanzhong's favor; a memorial proposed appointing him Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 樞曰：「廷范勳臣，幸有方鎮，何籍樂卿！

translations.literal: Shu said: "Tingfan is a meritorious minister who fortunately already holds a circuit governorship—what need has he of the Director of Music!"
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shu said, "Tingfan is a meritorious minister who already holds a provincial command—what need has he of the Court of Music!"

sentences.zh: 恐非元帥之旨。

translations.literal: I fear this is not the marshal's intent."
translations.idiomatic: I doubt this reflects the marshal's wishes."

sentences.zh: 」持之不下。

translations.literal: " He held to this and would not issue the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: " He held firm and refused to issue the appointment.

sentences.zh: 全忠聞之，謂賓佐曰：「吾常以裴十四器識真純，不入浮薄之黨，觀此議論，本態露矣。

translations.literal: Quanzhong heard of it and said to his retainers: "I have always regarded Pei Fourteen's talent and judgment as truly pure—that he would not join the frivolous faction; seeing this discussion, his true character is revealed."
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong heard of this, he told his staff, "I have always thought Pei Fourteen's character pure and his judgment sound—that he would not join the frivolous crowd. This argument shows his true colors."

sentences.zh: 」璨因此並遠、損譖於全忠，故三人皆罷。

translations.literal: " Can thereupon slandered Yuan and Sun as well before Quanzhong, and so all three were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " Because of this, Can also slandered Cui Yuan and Dugu Sun to Quanzhong, and all three were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 以吏部侍郎楊涉同平章事。

translations.literal: Yang She, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was made Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Yang She, Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was appointed Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 涉，收之孫也，為人和厚恭謹，聞當為相，與家人相泣，謂其子凝式曰：「此吾家之不幸也，必為汝累。

translations.literal: She was Yang Shou's grandson—by nature mild, generous, respectful, and cautious. When he heard he was to become chancellor, he wept with his family and said to his son Ningshi: "This is our family's misfortune—it is sure to bring trouble upon you."
translations.idiomatic: Yang She was Yang Shou's grandson—a mild, respectful, and cautious man. When he learned he was to become chancellor, he wept with his family and told his son Ningshi, "This is a calamity for our house—it will surely bring ruin upon you."

sentences.zh: 為清海節度使劉隱同平章事。

translations.literal: Liu Yin, military governor of Qinghai, was made Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yin, military governor of Qinghai, was appointed Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，河東都押牙蓋寓卒，遺書勸李克用省營繕，薄賦斂，求賢俊。

translations.literal: On renchen, Gai Yu, chief adjutant of Hedong, died; in a final letter he urged Li Keyong to reduce construction and repairs, lighten levies and taxes, and seek worthy and talented men.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Gai Yu, chief adjutant of Hedong, died. In a final letter he urged Li Keyong to cut back on construction, lighten taxes, and seek out able men.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚子，有彗星出西北。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on gengzi, a comet appeared in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on gengzi, a comet appeared in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 淮南將陶雅會衢、睦兵攻婺州，錢鏐遣其弟鏢將兵救之。

translations.literal: The Huainan general Tao Ya united troops from Qu and Mu to attack Wuzhou; Qian Liu sent his younger brother Biao with troops to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan general Tao Ya combined forces from Quzhou and Muzhou to attack Wuzhou. Qian Liu sent his younger brother Biao with an army to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 五月，禮院奏，皇帝登位應祀南郊，敕用十月甲午行之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Board of Rites memorialized that, upon the emperor's accession, the Southern Suburban Sacrifice should be performed; an edict fixed it for the tenth month, on jiawu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the Board of Rites reported that the emperor's accession required a sacrifice at the Southern Suburb; an edict scheduled it for jiawu in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，彗星長竟天。

translations.literal: On yichou, the comet stretched its length across the entire sky.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, the comet stretched across the entire sky.

sentences.zh: 柳璨恃朱全忠之勢，姿為威福。

translations.literal: Liu Can relied on Zhu Quanzhong's power and arbitrarily wielded authority for reward and punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can, relying on Zhu Quanzhong's power, wielded reward and punishment as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 會有星變，占者曰：「君臣俱災，宜誅殺以應之。

translations.literal: There chanced to be a change in the stars; diviners said: "Ruler and ministers alike face calamity—it is fitting to execute people to answer it."
translations.idiomatic: A celestial anomaly appeared, and diviners said, "Calamity threatens both ruler and ministers—the proper response is executions."

sentences.zh: 」璨因疏其素所不快者於全忠曰：「此曹皆聚徒橫議，怨望腹非，宜以之塞災異。

translations.literal: " Can thereupon listed before Quanzhong those he had long resented and said: "These men all gather followers and speak recklessly, harboring resentment and inwardly criticizing—they should be used to stave off the omen."
translations.idiomatic: " Can then reported to Quanzhong a list of men he had long resented, saying, "These men band together and speak recklessly, nursing grievances and secretly criticizing the court—they should serve to answer the omen."

sentences.zh: 」李振亦言於朱全忠曰：「朝廷所以不理，良由衣冠浮薄之徒紊亂綱紀；

translations.literal: " Li Zhen also said to Zhu Quanzhong: "The reason the court can achieve nothing is truly that frivolous men of the scholar-official class have thrown the order of the state into chaos;"
translations.idiomatic: " Li Zhen also told Zhu Quanzhong, "The court is paralyzed because frivolous scholars and officials have thrown the state into disorder;"

sentences.zh: 且王欲圖大事，此曹皆朝廷之難制者也，不若盡去之。

translations.literal: moreover, if Your Highness wishes to accomplish great affairs, these men are all hard for the court to control—better to remove them all."
translations.idiomatic: and if Your Highness means to accomplish great things, these are precisely the men the court cannot control. Better to remove them all."

sentences.zh: 」全忠以為然。

translations.literal: " Quanzhong thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong agreed.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，貶獨孤損為棣州刺史，裴樞為登州刺史，崔遠為萊州刺史。

translations.literal: On guiyou, Dugu Sun was demoted to prefect of Di, Pei Shu to prefect of Deng, and Cui Yuan to prefect of Lai.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Dugu Sun was demoted to prefect of Di Prefecture, Pei Shu to prefect of Deng, and Cui Yuan to prefect of Lai.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，貶吏部尚書陸扆為濮州司戶，工部尚書王溥為淄州司戶。

translations.literal: On yihai, Lu Yi, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was demoted to Registrar of Households at Puzhou; Wang Pu, Director of the Ministry of Works, was demoted to Registrar of Households at Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Lu Yi, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, was demoted to registrar of households at Puzhou, and Wang Pu, Director of the Ministry of Works, to the same post at Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，貶太子太保致仕趙崇為曹州司戶，兵部侍郎王贊為濰州司戶。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Zhao Chong, retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, was demoted to Registrar of Households at Caozhou; Wang Zan, Vice Director of the Ministry of War, was demoted to Registrar of Households at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Zhao Chong, the retired Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, was demoted to registrar of households at Caozhou, and Wang Zan, Vice Director of the Ministry of War, to the same at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 自餘或門冑高華，或科第自進，居三省台閣，以名檢自處，聲跡稍著者，皆指以為浮薄，貶逐無虛日，搢紳為之一空。

translations.literal: As for the rest—whether of lofty lineage or risen through the examinations, holding posts in the Three Departments and the Censorate and Secretariat, conducting themselves with regard for reputation—whoever was at all notable was denounced as frivolous; demotions and banishments came day after day without respite, and the scholar-official class was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whether of eminent birth or risen through the examinations, anyone in the Three Departments or secretariat who conducted himself with regard for reputation and had made any mark at all was denounced as frivolous. Demotions and banishments came day after day without pause until the scholar-official class was nearly emptied.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，再貶裴樞為瀧州司戶，獨孤損為瓊州司戶，崔遠為白州司戶。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Pei Shu was demoted again to Registrar of Households at Longzhou, Dugu Sun to Registrar of Households at Qiongzhou, and Cui Yuan to Registrar of Households at Baizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Pei Shu was demoted again to registrar of households at Longzhou, Dugu Sun to the same at Qiongzhou, and Cui Yuan to the same at Baizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲申，忠義節度使趙匡凝遣使修好於王建。

translations.literal: On jiashen, Zhao Kuangning, military governor of Zhongyi, sent envoys to establish friendly relations with Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Zhao Kuangning, military governor of Zhongyi, sent envoys to seek friendly relations with Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 六月，戊子朔，敕裴樞、獨孤損、崔遠、陸扆、王溥、趙崇、王贊等並所在賜自盡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the wuzi new moon, an edict ordered that Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, Cui Yuan, Lu Yi, Wang Pu, Zhao Chong, Wang Zan, and the rest be granted death by their own hand wherever they were.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the wuzi new moon, an edict granted Pei Shu, Dugu Sun, Cui Yuan, Lu Yi, Wang Pu, Zhao Chong, Wang Zan, and the others permission to take their own lives wherever they were stationed.

sentences.zh: 時全忠聚樞等及朝士貶官者三十餘人於白馬驛，一夕盡殺之，投屍於河。

translations.literal: At the time Quanzhong gathered Shu and the others and more than thirty demoted court officials at White Horse Post; in one night he killed them all and threw their bodies into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong had gathered Pei Shu and more than thirty other demoted officials at White Horse Post and killed them all in a single night, throwing their bodies into the river.

sentences.zh: 初，李振屢舉進士，竟不中第，故深疾搢紳之士，言於全忠曰：「此輩常自謂清流，宜投之黃河，使為濁流！

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Zhen had repeatedly taken the jinshi examination but never passed; he therefore deeply hated scholar-officials. He said to Quanzhong: "These men always call themselves the clear stream—they ought to be cast into the Yellow River and become part of the muddy flow!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen had repeatedly sat for the jinshi examination without ever passing, and he therefore deeply resented scholar-officials. He told Quanzhong, "These men call themselves the 'clear stream'—they ought to be thrown into the Yellow River and made part of the muddy flow!"

sentences.zh: 」全忠笑而從之。

translations.literal: " Quanzhong laughed and complied.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong laughed and agreed.

sentences.zh: 振每自汴至洛，朝廷必有竄逐者，時人謂之鴟梟。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhen came from Bian to Luoyang, the court always had someone banished; contemporaries called him "the owl and the kite."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhen traveled from Bian to Luoyang, someone at court was always banished, and contemporaries called him "the owl and the kite."

sentences.zh: 見朝士皆頤指氣使，旁若無人。

translations.literal: When he saw court officials he ordered them about arrogantly, as though no one else were present.
translations.idiomatic: In the presence of court officials he ordered them about with arrogant contempt, as if no one else were there.

sentences.zh: 全忠嘗與僚佐及遊客坐於大柳之下，全忠獨言曰：「此木宜為車轂。

translations.literal: Quanzhong once sat with his staff and visiting guests beneath a great willow tree. Quanzhong alone said: "This wood would be fit for cart hubs."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong once sat with his staff and guests beneath a great willow. He remarked alone, "This wood would do nicely for cart hubs."

sentences.zh: 」眾莫應。

translations.literal: " No one responded.
translations.idiomatic: " No one replied.

sentences.zh: 有遊客數人起應曰：「宜為車轂。

translations.literal: Several visiting guests rose and answered: "It would be fit for cart hubs."
translations.idiomatic: Several guests rose and answered, "It would make fine cart hubs."

sentences.zh: 」全忠勃然厲聲曰：「書生輩好順口玩人，皆此類也！

translations.literal: " Quanzhong suddenly flushed and said in a harsh voice: "Men of letters love to flatter with their mouths and toy with people—all are of this sort!"
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong flushed with anger and said sharply, "Scholars love to flatter with their mouths and toy with people—they are all like this!"

sentences.zh: 」車轂須用夾榆，柳木豈可為之！

translations.literal: " Cart hubs require layered elm—how could willow wood serve!"
translations.idiomatic: " Cart hubs require layered elm—willow wood is no use for that!"

sentences.zh: 」顧左右曰：「尚何待！

translations.literal: " He turned to those beside him and said: "What are you waiting for!"
translations.idiomatic: " He turned to his attendants and said, "What are you waiting for!"

sentences.zh: 」左右數十人捽言「宜為車轂」者，悉撲殺之。

translations.literal: " Several dozen attendants seized those who had said "fit for cart hubs" and beat them all to death.
translations.idiomatic: " Dozens of attendants seized the men who had said the wood would make cart hubs and beat them all to death.

sentences.zh: 己丑，司空致仕裴贄貶青州司戶，尋賜死。

translations.literal: On jichou, Pei Zan, retired Minister of Works, was demoted to Registrar of Households at Qingzhou; soon he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Pei Zan, the retired Minister of Works, was demoted to registrar of households at Qingzhou and soon afterward granted death.

sentences.zh: 柳璨餘怒所注，猶不啻十數，張文蔚力解之，乃止。

translations.literal: Liu Can's lingering anger still had more than a dozen targets; Zhang Wenwei strenuously interceded, and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can's rage still had more than a dozen targets in view, but Zhang Wenwei argued strenuously on their behalf and at last he desisted.

sentences.zh: 時士大夫避亂，多不入朝。

translations.literal: At the time scholar-officials fleeing the turmoil mostly did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many scholar-officials, fleeing the chaos, stayed away from court.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，敕所在州縣督遣，無得稽留。

translations.literal: On renchen, an edict ordered every prefecture and county to press them to depart and forbade delay.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, an edict ordered local prefectures and counties to press them to report and forbade any delay.

sentences.zh: 前司勳員外郎李延古，德裕之孫也，去官居平泉莊，詔下未至。

translations.literal: The former Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Merits Li Yanggu was the grandson of Li Deyu; he had left office and lived at the Pingquan estate—the edict was issued but he had not yet arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanggu, a former Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Merits and grandson of Li Deyu, had left office and was living at his Pingquan estate when the edict was issued, but he had not yet reported.

sentences.zh: 戊申，責授衛尉寺主簿。

translations.literal: On wushen, he was punished by appointment as Chief Clerk of the Court of Imperial Carriages.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, he was punished with appointment as chief clerk of the Court of Imperial Carriages.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸亥，太子賓客致仕柳遜貶曹州司馬。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on guihai, Liu Xun, retired Consultant to the Heir Apparent, was demoted to Vice-Military Administrator of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, on guihai, Liu Xun, the retired Consultant to the Heir Apparent, was demoted to vice-military administrator of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 庚午夜，天雄牙將李公佺與牙軍謀亂，羅紹威覺之；

translations.literal: At midnight on gengwu, Li Gongxian, a junior officer of the Tianxiong command, plotted rebellion with the guard army; Luo Shaowei discovered it;
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on gengwu, Li Gongxian, a Tianxiong guard officer, plotted mutiny with the army guard; Luo Shaowei discovered the plot;

sentences.zh: 公佺焚府捨，剽掠，奔滄州。

translations.literal: Gongxian burned the headquarters buildings, plundered, and fled to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gongxian set fire to the headquarters, looted the city, and fled to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，王建遣前山南西道節度使王宗賀等將兵，擊昭信節度使馮行襲於金州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Wang Jian sent the former military governor of Shannan West Wang Zonghe and others with troops to attack Feng Xingsi, military governor of Zhaoxin, at Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Wang Jian sent Wang Zonghe, former military governor of Shannan West, and others to attack Feng Xingsi, military governor of Zhaoxin, at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠以趙匡凝東與楊行密交通，西與王建結婚，乙未，遣武寧節度使楊師厚將兵擊之，己亥，全忠以大軍繼之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong, because Zhao Kuangning had dealings with Yang Xingmi in the east and a marriage alliance with Wang Jian in the west, on yiwei sent Yang Shihou, military governor of Wuning, with troops to attack him; on jihai Quanzhong followed with a great army.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhao Kuangning was in contact with Yang Xingmi to the east and allied by marriage with Wang Jian to the west, Zhu Quanzhong on yiwei sent Yang Shihou, military governor of Wuning, against him with an army, and on jihai followed with the main force.

sentences.zh: 處州刺史盧約使其弟佶攻陷溫州，張惠奔福州。

translations.literal: Lu Yue, prefect of Chuzhou, had his younger brother Ji attack and take Wenzhou; Zhang Hui fled to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yue, prefect of Chuzhou, had his younger brother Ji capture Wenzhou, and Zhang Hui fled to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐遣方永珍救婺州。

translations.literal: Qian Liu sent Fang Yongzhen to rescue Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent Fang Yongzhen to relieve Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，禮部員外郎知制詔司空圖棄官居虞鄉王官谷，昭宗屢征之，不起。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sikong Tu, Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and Drafting Secretary, had abandoned office and lived at Wangguan Valley in Yuxiang; Emperor Zhaozong repeatedly summoned him, but he would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Sikong Tu, Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and Drafting Secretary, had resigned and was living at Wangguan Valley in Yuxiang. Emperor Zhaozong repeatedly summoned him, but he refused to come.

sentences.zh: 柳璨以詔書征之，圖懼，詣洛陽入見，陽為衰野，墜笏失儀。

translations.literal: Liu Can summoned him by imperial edict; Tu was afraid, went to Luoyang to have an audience, and feigned senility and rusticity, dropping his tablet and losing deportment.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can summoned him by edict. Tu was frightened, went to Luoyang for an audience, and feigned feebleness and rustic ignorance, dropping his court tablet and making a spectacle of himself.

sentences.zh: 璨乃復下詔，略曰：「既養高以傲代，類移山以釣名。

translations.literal: Can then issued another edict, in part reading: "Having cultivated loftiness to scorn the age, you are like one who moved a mountain to fish for fame."
translations.idiomatic: Can then issued another edict that read in part, "Having cultivated lofty retirement to scorn the age, you are like someone who moved a mountain merely to fish for a name."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「匪夷匪惠，難居公正之朝。

translations.literal: " It also said: "Neither foreign barbarian nor benefactor—you are hard to keep in a court of upright fairness."
translations.idiomatic: " It also said, "Neither foreigner nor benefactor—you cannot remain in a court devoted to justice."

sentences.zh: 可放還山。

translations.literal: You may be released to return to the mountains."
translations.idiomatic: You are dismissed to return to the mountains."

sentences.zh: 」圖，臨淮人也。

translations.literal: " Tu was a man of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: " Tu was a native of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 楊師厚攻下唐、鄧、復、郢、隨、均、房七州，朱全忠軍於漢北。

translations.literal: Yang Shihou captured the seven prefectures of Tang, Deng, Fu, Ying, Sui, Jun, and Fang; Zhu Quanzhong encamped north of the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shihou captured the seven prefectures of Tang, Deng, Fu, Ying, Sui, Jun, and Fang, while Zhu Quanzhong camped north of the Han.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛酉，命師厚作浮梁於陰谷口，癸亥，引兵渡漢。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinyou, he ordered Shihou to build a pontoon bridge at the mouth of Yingu Valley; on guihai he led troops across the Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinyou, he ordered Shihou to build a pontoon bridge at the mouth of Yingu Valley. On guihai he led his army across the Han.

sentences.zh: 甲子，趙匡凝將兵二萬陳於漢濱，師厚與戰，大破之，遂傅其城下。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Zhao Kuangning arrayed twenty thousand troops on the bank of the Han; Shihou battled him, routed him utterly, and pressed to the foot of his walls.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Zhao Kuangning drew up twenty thousand men on the Han's bank. Shihou engaged him, routed his army utterly, and pressed his attack to the walls of the city.

sentences.zh: 是夕，匡凝焚府城，帥其族及麾下士沿漢奔廣陵。

translations.literal: That evening Kuangning burned the headquarters city, led his clan and the troops under his command along the Han, and fled to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: That night Kuangning burned the headquarters city and fled along the Han to Guangling with his clan and his followers.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，師厚入襄陽；

translations.literal: On yichou, Shihou entered Xiangyang;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Shihou entered Xiangyang;

sentences.zh: 丙寓，全忠繼至。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Quanzhong arrived in succession.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Quanzhong arrived in turn.

sentences.zh: 匡凝至廣陵，楊行密戲之曰：「君在鎮，歲以金帛輸朱全忠，今敗，乃歸我乎？

translations.literal: When Kuangning reached Guangling, Yang Xingmi bantered with him, saying: "When you held your command, you sent gold and silks every year to Zhu Quanzhong; now that you are defeated, you come to me?"
translations.idiomatic: When Kuangning reached Guangling, Yang Xingmi taunted him, saying, "In your command you sent gold and silk every year to Zhu Quanzhong—now that you are beaten, you come to me?"

sentences.zh: 」匡凝曰：「諸侯事天子，歲輸貢賦乃其職也，豈輸賊乎！

translations.literal: " Kuangning said: "When feudatories serve the Son of Heaven, sending annual tribute and levies is their duty—how could that be sending goods to a rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: " Kuangning replied, "When lords serve the emperor, sending annual tribute is their duty—how could that be supplying a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 今日歸公，正以不從賊故耳。

translations.literal: Today I come to Your Lordship precisely because I would not follow the rebel."
translations.idiomatic: I come to you today precisely because I refused to serve the rebel."

sentences.zh: 」行密厚遇之。

translations.literal: " Xingmi treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingmi treated him with great hospitality.

sentences.zh: 封皇弟禔為穎王，祐為蔡王。

translations.literal: The emperor's younger brother Ti was enfeoffed as Prince of Ying, and You as Prince of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's younger brother Ti was enfeoffed as Prince of Ying and You as Prince of Cai.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，荊南節度使趙匡明帥眾二萬，棄城奔成都。

translations.literal: On dingmao, Zhao Kuangming, military governor of Jingnan, led twenty thousand men, abandoned his city, and fled to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Zhao Kuangming, military governor of Jingnan, abandoned his city with twenty thousand men and fled to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，朱全忠以楊師厚為山南東道留後，引兵擊江陵。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Zhu Quanzhong made Yang Shihou regent of Shannan East Circuit and led troops to attack Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Zhu Quanzhong appointed Yang Shihou regent of Shannan East Circuit and marched to attack Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 至樂鄉，荊南牙將王建武遣使迎降。

translations.literal: Reaching Ledistrict, Jingnan's junior general Wang Jianwu sent envoys to welcome him and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Ledistrict, Wang Jianwu, a junior general of Jingnan, sent envoys to welcome him and surrender.

sentences.zh: 全忠以都將賀瑰為荊南留後。

translations.literal: Quanzhong made his commandery general He Gui regent of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong appointed his commandery general He Gui regent of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 全忠尋表師厚為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong soon memorialized to make Shihou military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong soon submitted a memorial to appoint Shihou military governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 王宗賀等攻馮行襲，所向皆捷。

translations.literal: Wang Zonghe and others attacked Feng Xingxi; wherever they went they were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zonghe and others attacked Feng Xingxi and won every engagement.

sentences.zh: 丙子，行襲棄金州，奔均州。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Xingxi abandoned Jin Prefecture and fled to Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Xingxi abandoned Jin Prefecture and fled to Jun.

sentences.zh: 其將全師朗以城降。

translations.literal: His general Quan Shilang surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: His general Quan Shilang surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 王建更師朗姓名曰王宗朗，補金州觀察使，割渠、巴、開三州以隸之。

translations.literal: Wang Jian changed Shilang's surname and personal name to Wang Zonglang, appointed him observation commissioner of Jin Prefecture, and carved off the three prefectures of Qu, Ba, and Kai to make them subordinate to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian renamed Shilang Wang Zonglang, made him observation commissioner of Jin Prefecture, and detached the three prefectures of Qu, Ba, and Kai to place under his authority.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔更用十一月癸酉親郊。

translations.literal: On yiyou, an edict changed the imperial suburban sacrifice to guiyou in the eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, an edict rescheduled the imperial suburban sacrifice to guiyou in the eleventh month.

sentences.zh: 淮南將陶雅、陳璋拔婺州，執刺史沈夏以歸。

translations.literal: Huainan's generals Tao Ya and Chen Zhang captured Wuzhou, seized Prefect Shen Xia, and returned with him.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan generals Tao Ya and Chen Zhang took Wuzhou, seized Prefect Shen Xia, and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 楊行密以雅為江南都招討使，歙、婺、衢、睦觀察使，以璋為衢、婺副招討使。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi made Ya overall Jiangnan suppression commissioner and observation commissioner of She, Wu, Qu, and Mu; he made Zhang deputy suppression commissioner of Qu and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi appointed Ya overall Jiangnan suppression commissioner and observation commissioner of She, Wu, Qu, and Mu, and made Zhang deputy suppression commissioner for Qu and Wu.

sentences.zh: 璋攻暨陽，兩浙將方習敗之。

translations.literal: Zhang attacked Jiyang; Fang Xi, a general of the Two Zhes, defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang attacked Jiyang, but Fang Xi, a general of the Two Zhes, defeated him.

sentences.zh: 習進攻婺州。

translations.literal: Xi advanced to attack Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi then pressed the attack on Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 濠州團練使劉金卒，楊行密以金子仁規知濠州。

translations.literal: Liu Jin, regimental commissioner of Haozhou, died; Yang Xingmi made Jin's son Ren Gui acting prefect of Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin, regimental commissioner of Haozhou, died. Yang Xingmi put Jin's son Ren Gui in charge of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 楊行密長子宣州觀察使渥，素無令譽，軍府輕之。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi's eldest son Wo, observation commissioner of Xuanzhou, had never had a good reputation; the headquarters looked down on him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi's eldest son Wo, observation commissioner of Xuanzhou, had never enjoyed a good reputation, and the headquarters held him in low regard.

sentences.zh: 行密寢疾，命節度判官周隱召渥。

translations.literal: Xingmi took to his bed with illness and ordered his military-governor's aide Zhou Yin to summon Wo.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi fell gravely ill, he ordered his military-governor's aide Zhou Yin to summon Wo.

sentences.zh: 隱性憃直，對曰：「宣州司徒輕易信讒，喜擊球飲酒，非保家之主。

translations.literal: Yin was by nature simple and blunt; he replied: "The Xuanzhou grand commandant is rash and easily trusts slander, delights in polo and drinking wine—not one to preserve a house."
translations.idiomatic: Yin was blunt and plainspoken by nature. He replied, "The grand commandant of Xuanzhou is rash and credulous of slander, fond of polo and wine—not a man to preserve the family estate."

sentences.zh: 餘子皆幼，未能駕馭諸將。

translations.literal: The remaining sons are all young and cannot yet control the generals.
translations.idiomatic: The other sons are all still young and cannot yet command the generals.

sentences.zh: 廬州刺史劉威，從王起細微，必不負王，不若使之權領軍府，俟諸子長以授之。

translations.literal: Liu Wei, prefect of Luzhou, rose with the Prince from obscurity and would certainly not betray him; better to have him rule the headquarters in an acting capacity and wait until the sons grow up to invest them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei, prefect of Luzhou, rose with you from humble beginnings and would surely not betray you. Better to have him govern the headquarters provisionally and invest your sons when they come of age.

sentences.zh: 」行密不應。

translations.literal: " Xingmi did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Xingmi made no reply.

sentences.zh: 左右牙指揮使徐溫、張顥言於行密曰：「王平生出萬死，冒矢石，為子孫立基業，安可使他人有之！

translations.literal: The left and right fang-army commanders Xu Wen and Zhang Hao said to Xingmi: "Your Highness in a lifetime passed through ten thousand deaths and braved arrows and stones to establish an estate for your descendants—how can we let another have it!"
translations.idiomatic: The left and right fang-army commanders Xu Wen and Zhang Hao said to Xingmi, "Your Highness risked death a thousand times in battle and braved arrows and stones to build this estate for your descendants—how can we let another take it!"

sentences.zh: 」行密曰：「吾死瞑目矣！

translations.literal: " Xingmi said: "When I die I shall close my eyes in peace!"
translations.idiomatic: " Xingmi said, "Then I can die in peace!"

sentences.zh: 」隱，舒州人也。

translations.literal: " Yin was a man of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Yin was a native of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 他日，將佐問疾，行密目留幕僚嚴可求。

translations.literal: Another day, generals and aides came to inquire after his illness; Xingmi signaled with his eyes to keep staff member Yan Keqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On another day, when generals and aides came to inquire after his health, Xingmi signaled with his eyes for staff member Yan Keqiu to remain.

sentences.zh: 眾出，可求曰：「王若不諱，如軍府何？

translations.literal: When the rest had gone out, Keqiu said: "If Your Highness does not recover, what of the headquarters?"
translations.idiomatic: After the others had left, Keqiu said, "If Your Highness does not recover, what will become of the headquarters?"

sentences.zh: 」行密曰：「吾命周隱召渥，今忍死待之。

translations.literal: " Xingmi said: "I ordered Zhou Yin to summon Wo; now I endure death waiting for him."
translations.idiomatic: " Xingmi said, "I ordered Zhou Yin to summon Wo. I am clinging to life to wait for him."

sentences.zh: 」可求與徐溫詣隱，隱未出見，牒猶在案上，可求即與溫取牒，遣使者如宣州召之。

translations.literal: " Keqiu and Xu Wen went to Yin; Yin had not yet come out to see them, and the dispatch was still on the desk. Keqiu immediately took the dispatch with Wen and sent a messenger to Xuanzhou to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: " Keqiu and Xu Wen went to Yin. Yin had not yet come out to receive them, but the dispatch was still on his desk. Keqiu and Wen at once took it and sent a messenger to Xuanzhou to summon Wo.

sentences.zh: 可求，同州人也。

translations.literal: Keqiu was a man of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Keqiu was a native of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 行密以潤州團練使王茂章為宣州觀察使。

translations.literal: Xingmi made Wang Maozhang, regimental commissioner of Runzhou, observation commissioner of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi appointed Wang Maozhang, regimental commissioner of Runzhou, observation commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙戌朔，以朱全忠為諸道兵馬元帥，別開幕府。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingwu, the new moon, Zhu Quanzhong was made commander-in-chief of all circuits' armies and horses and separately opened a field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the bingwu new moon, Zhu Quanzhong was appointed commander-in-chief of all circuits' armies and opened a separate field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 是日，全忠部署將士，將歸大梁，忽變計，欲乘勝擊淮南。

translations.literal: That day Quanzhong deployed officers and troops, intending to return to Daliang, but suddenly changed plan and wished to exploit victory to strike Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Quanzhong mustered his officers and troops to return to Daliang, but suddenly changed plan and decided to press the victory against Huainan.

sentences.zh: 敬翔諫曰：「今出師未逾月，平兩大鎮，闢地數千里，遠近聞之，莫不震懾。

translations.literal: Jing Xiang remonstrated, saying: "Now the expedition has not passed a month; you have pacified two great circuits and opened territory several thousand li—near and far who hear of it none who are not awed and shaken."
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang remonstrated, "Your campaign has not yet lasted a month. You have subdued two great circuits and seized territory for thousands of li. Near and far, all who hear of it are awestruck."

sentences.zh: 此威望可惜，不若且歸息兵，俟釁而動。

translations.literal: This prestige is a pity to waste; better for now to return and rest the troops and wait for an opening before acting.
translations.idiomatic: It would be a shame to squander this prestige. Better to return for now, rest the army, and wait for an opening.

sentences.zh: 」不聽。

translations.literal: " He did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 改昭信軍為戎昭軍。

translations.literal: Zhao Xin Army was renamed Rong Zhao Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhao Xin Army was renamed the Rong Zhao Army.

sentences.zh: 仍割均州隸之。

translations.literal: Jun Prefecture was still carved off and made subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: Jun Prefecture was also detached and placed under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，朱全忠發襄州。

translations.literal: On xinmao, Zhu Quanzhong set out from Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Zhu Quanzhong marched out from Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，至棗陽，遇大雨。

translations.literal: On renchen, he reached Zaoyang and encountered heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen he reached Zaoyang in heavy rain.

sentences.zh: 自申州抵光州，道險狹塗潦，人馬疲乏，士卒尚未冬服，多逃亡。

translations.literal: From Shen Prefecture to Guang Prefecture the road was treacherous, narrow, and mired; men and horses were exhausted; the soldiers still lacked winter clothing, and many fled.
translations.idiomatic: From Shenzhou to Guangzhou the route was treacherous, narrow, and waterlogged. Men and horses were exhausted, the soldiers still lacked winter clothing, and many deserted.

sentences.zh: 全忠使人謂光州刺史柴再用曰：「下，我以汝為蔡州刺史；

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent someone to tell Chai Zaiyong, prefect of Guang Prefecture: "If you surrender, I will make you prefect of Cai Prefecture;"
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent a messenger to Chai Zaiyong, prefect of Guangzhou, saying, "Surrender, and I will make you prefect of Caizhou;"

sentences.zh: 不下，且屠城！

translations.literal: if you do not surrender, I will sack the city!"
translations.idiomatic: refuse, and I will slaughter the city!"

sentences.zh: 」再用嚴設守備，戎服登城，見全忠，拜伏甚恭，曰：「光州城小兵弱，不足以辱王之威怒。

translations.literal: " Zaiyong strictly set defenses, donned armor and mounted the wall, saw Quanzhong, bowed prostrate very respectfully, and said: "Guang Prefecture's walls are small and its troops few—not enough to suffer Your Highness's awesome wrath."
translations.idiomatic: " Zaiyong made his defenses tight, donned armor, mounted the wall, and when he saw Quanzhong bowed low and said respectfully, "Guangzhou is small and weak—not worthy of Your Highness's wrath."

sentences.zh: 王苟先下壽州，敢不從命。

translations.literal: If Your Highness will first take Shou Prefecture, I dare not disobey your command."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness takes Shouzhou first, I shall not fail to obey."

sentences.zh: 」全忠留其城東旬日而去。

translations.literal: " Quanzhong remained east of the city ten days and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong camped east of the city for ten days and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 起居郎蘇楷，禮部尚書循之子也，素無才行，乾寧中登進士第，昭宗覆試黜之，仍永不聽入科場。

translations.literal: Attendant Su Kai, son of Minister of Rites Su Xun, had never had ability or conduct; in the Qianning era he passed the jinshi examination, but Emperor Zhaozong in a re-examination dismissed him and furthermore forever barred him from the examination halls.
