translations.idiomatic: Attendant Su Kai, son of Minister of Rites Su Xun, had never shown talent or character. During Qianning he passed the jinshi examination, but Emperor Zhaozong failed him on re-examination and permanently barred him from the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 甲午，楷帥同列上言：「謚號美惡，臣子不得而私，先帝謚號多溢美，乞更詳議。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Kai led his colleagues in a memorial: "Posthumous titles' praise and blame—subjects may not treat as private matter; the late emperor's posthumous title has much excess praise; we beg a fuller reconsideration."
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Kai led his colleagues in submitting a memorial: "Whether a posthumous title is flattering or condemnatory is not for subjects to decide privately. The late emperor's title is excessively flattering. We beg that it be reconsidered in full."

sentences.zh: 」事下太常，丁酉，張廷范奏改謚恭靈莊愍孝皇帝，廟號襄宗，詔從之。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites; on dingyou, Zhang Tingfan memorialized to change the posthumous title to Emperor Gongling Zhuangmin Xiao, temple name Xiangzong, and an edict followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites. On dingyou, Zhang Tingfan memorialized to change the posthumous title to Emperor Gongling Zhuangmin Xiao, with temple name Xiangzong, and an edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 楊渥至廣陵。

translations.literal: Yang Wo reached Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wo arrived at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，楊行密承製以渥為淮南留後。

translations.literal: On xinchou, Yang Xingmi, acting on imperial commission, made Wo regent of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Yang Xingmi, acting under imperial commission, appointed Wo regent of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 戊申，朱全忠發光州，迷失道百餘里，又遇雨，比及壽州，壽人堅壁清野以待之。

translations.literal: On wushen, Zhu Quanzhong set out from Guang Prefecture, lost the road for more than a hundred li, and again encountered rain; by the time he reached Shou Prefecture, the people of Shou had sealed their walls and cleared the countryside awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Zhu Quanzhong marched out from Guangzhou, lost his way for more than a hundred li, and ran into rain again. By the time he reached Shouzhou, the people there had sealed their walls and stripped the countryside bare in anticipation.

sentences.zh: 全忠欲圍之，無林木可為柵，乃退屯正陽。

translations.literal: Quanzhong wished to besiege it but had no timber to make palisades; he then withdrew and encamped at Zhengyang.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong wanted to besiege the city but found no timber for palisades, so he withdrew and encamped at Zhengyang.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，更名成德軍曰武順。

translations.literal: On guichou, the Chengde Army was renamed Wushun.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, the Chengde Army was renamed Wushun.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙辰，朱全忠渡淮而北，柴再用抄其後軍，斬首三千級，獲輜重萬計。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on bingchen, Zhu Quanzhong crossed the Huai northward; Chai Zaiyong raided his rear army, beheaded three thousand ranks, and captured baggage and heavy stores numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on bingchen, Zhu Quanzhong crossed the Huai and marched north. Chai Zaiyong struck his rear guard, took three thousand heads, and seized vast amounts of baggage and supplies.

sentences.zh: 全忠悔之，躁忿尤甚。

translations.literal: Quanzhong regretted it and was all the more irritable and angry.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong bitterly regretted the campaign and grew still more furious.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，至大梁。

translations.literal: On dingmao, he reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao he reached Daliang.

sentences.zh: 先是，全忠急於傳禪，密使蔣玄暉等謀之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Quanzhong was eager to transfer the throne and secretly sent Jiang Xuanhui and others to plan it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Quanzhong was eager to have the throne abdicated to him and secretly sent Jiang Xuanhui and others to arrange it.

sentences.zh: 玄暉與柳璨等議：以魏、晉以來皆先封大國，加九錫，殊禮，然後受禪，當次第行之。

translations.literal: Xuanhui discussed with Liu Can and others: since Wei and Jin, all had first been enfeoffed with a great state, given the Nine Bestowals and special honors, and only then received the abdication—it should be carried out step by step.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui discussed with Liu Can and others that since Wei and Jin, every usurper had first been enfeoffed with a great state, granted the Nine Bestowals and special honors, and only then received the abdication. They should proceed in that order.

sentences.zh: 乃先除全忠諸道元帥，以示有漸，仍以刑部尚書裴迪為送宮告使，全忠大怒。

translations.literal: They therefore first removed Quanzhong's title as commander-in-chief of all circuits to show gradual progress, and still made Pei Di, Minister of Justice, envoy to deliver the palace announcement—Quanzhong was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: They first stripped Quanzhong of his title as commander-in-chief of all circuits to show gradual progress, and still dispatched Pei Di, Minister of Justice, as envoy to deliver the palace announcement. Quanzhong was furious.

sentences.zh: 宣徽副使王殷、趙殷衡疾玄暉權寵，欲得其處，因譖之於全忠曰：「玄暉、璨等欲延唐祚，故逗遛其事以須變。

translations.literal: Deputy commissioners of the Palace Secretariat Wang Yin and Zhao Yinheng resented Xuanhui's power and favor and wanted his place; they therefore slandered him to Quanzhong, saying: "Xuanhui, Can, and the others wish to prolong Tang's fortune, and therefore delay the matter waiting for change."
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commissioners of the Palace Secretariat Wang Yin and Zhao Yinheng resented Xuanhui's power and favor and coveted his position. They slandered him to Quanzhong, saying, "Xuanhui, Can, and the others mean to prolong the Tang dynasty and are deliberately stalling, waiting for some turn of events."

sentences.zh: 」玄暉聞之懼，自至壽春，具言其狀。

translations.literal: " When Xuanhui heard of it he was afraid and went in person to Shouchun, fully explaining the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xuanhui heard this he was frightened and went in person to Shouchun to explain everything.

sentences.zh: 全忠曰：「汝曹巧述閒事以沮我，借使我不受九錫，豈不能作天子邪！

translations.literal: Quanzhong said: "You people cleverly invent trifling matters to obstruct me—even if I do not receive the Nine Bestowals, can I not still become Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong said, "You people invent petty excuses to block me. Even if I never receive the Nine Bestowals, can I not still become emperor?"

sentences.zh: 」玄暉曰：「唐祚已盡，天命歸王，愚智皆知之。

translations.literal: " Xuanhui said: "Tang's fortune is already spent; Heaven's mandate belongs to Your Highness—fool and wise alike know it."
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanhui said, "The Tang dynasty's mandate is spent. Heaven's favor rests with you—everyone knows it, wise and simple alike."

sentences.zh: 玄暉與柳璨等非敢有背德，但以今茲晉、燕、岐、蜀皆吾勍敵，王遽受禪，彼心未服，不可不曲盡義理，然後取之，欲為王創萬代之業耳。

translations.literal: Xuanhui and Liu Can and the others do not dare to be disloyal; it is only that now Jin, Yan, Qi, and Shu are all our strong foes—if Your Highness hastily receives the abdication, their hearts will not be won over; one cannot but thoroughly fulfill every propriety and only then take it, wishing to create an estate lasting ten thousand generations for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui and Liu Can are not disloyal. But Jin, Yan, Qi, and Shu are all formidable foes. If you accept the throne too hastily, they will not submit in heart. Every propriety must be observed before you take it—we mean only to secure an empire that will last ten thousand generations for you."

sentences.zh: 」全忠叱之曰：「奴果反矣！

translations.literal: " Quanzhong shouted at him: "The slave truly has rebelled!"
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong barked at him, "The slave really has turned traitor!"

sentences.zh: 」玄暉惶遽辭歸，與璨議行九錫。

translations.literal: " Xuanhui in panic and haste took leave and returned, and with Can discussed carrying out the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanhui fled in panic and returned to discuss the Nine Bestowals with Can.

sentences.zh: 時天子將郊祀，百官既習儀，裴迪自大梁還，言全忠怒曰：「柳璨、蔣玄暉等欲延唐祚，乃郊天也。

translations.literal: At the time the Son of Heaven was about to perform the suburban sacrifice; the hundred officials had already rehearsed the rites. Pei Di returned from Daliang and reported that Quanzhong angrily said: "Liu Can, Jiang Xuanhui, and the others wish to prolong Tang's fortune—so they are sacrificing to Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to perform the suburban sacrifice, and the officials had already rehearsed the rites. When Pei Di returned from Daliang, he reported that Quanzhong had raged, "Liu Can, Jiang Xuanhui, and the others mean to prolong the Tang—so they sacrifice to Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 」璨等懼，庚午，敕改用來年正月上辛。

translations.literal: " Can and the others were afraid; on gengwu, an edict changed it to the upper xin day of the first month of the coming year.
translations.idiomatic: " Can and the others were terrified. On gengwu, an edict rescheduled the ceremony for the upper xin day of the first month of the coming year.

sentences.zh: 殷衡本姓孔名循，為全忠家乳母養子，故冒姓趙，後漸貴，復其姓名。

translations.literal: Yinheng's original surname was Kong and personal name Xun; he was the foster son of Quanzhong's family's wet nurse, and therefore falsely took the surname Zhao; later he gradually rose in rank and restored his original surname and name.
translations.idiomatic: Yinheng's original name was Kong Xun. He had been adopted by the wet nurse of Quanzhong's household and had taken the surname Zhao, but as he rose in rank he restored his true name.

sentences.zh: 壬申，趙匡明至成都，王建以客禮遇之。

translations.literal: On renshen, Zhao Kuangming reached Chengdu; Wang Jian treated him with guest's courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Zhao Kuangming arrived at Chengdu, and Wang Jian received him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 昭宗之喪，朝廷遣告哀使司馬卿宣諭王建，至是始入蜀境。

translations.literal: At Emperor Zhaozong's mourning, the court dispatched mourning envoy Sima Qing to announce and instruct Wang Jian; only now did he first enter Shu territory.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhaozong's death, the court had sent mourning envoy Sima Qing to announce the news to Wang Jian. Only now did he enter Shu territory.

sentences.zh: 西川掌書記韋莊為建謀，使武定節度使王宗綰諭卿曰：「蜀之將士，世受唐恩，去歲聞乘輿東遷，凡上二十表，皆不報。

translations.literal: Wei Zhuang, chief secretary of Xichuan, plotted for Jian and had Wang Zongyan, military governor of Wuding, instruct Qing, saying: "Shu's officers and soldiers for generations received Tang's grace; last year hearing the imperial carriage moved east, we altogether submitted twenty memorials, all unanswered."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhuang, chief secretary of Xichuan, advised Wang Jian to have Wang Zongyan, military governor of Wuding, tell Qing, "Shu's officers and soldiers have owed their livelihood to the Tang for generations. Last year, when we heard the emperor had been taken east, we submitted twenty memorials, none of which received a reply."

sentences.zh: 尋有亡卒自汴來，聞先帝已罹朱全忠弒逆。

translations.literal: Soon a fugitive soldier came from Bian and reported that the late emperor had suffered Zhu Quanzhong's regicide and treason.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a deserter arrived from Bian with word that the late emperor had fallen victim to Zhu Quanzhong's murder and treason.

sentences.zh: 蜀之將士方日夕枕戈，思為先帝報仇。

translations.literal: Shu's officers and soldiers were just then night and day sleeping upon their weapons, thinking to avenge the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shu's soldiers now sleep with weapons at hand day and night, longing to avenge the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 不知今茲使來以何事宣諭？

translations.literal: We do not know for what matter the envoy comes now to announce and instruct?
translations.idiomatic: We do not know what message you bring on this visit.

sentences.zh: 舍人宜自圖進退。

translations.literal: Attendant, you should consider your own advance or retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant, you would do well to consider your next move."

sentences.zh: 」卿乃還。

translations.literal: " Qing then returned.
translations.idiomatic: " Qing turned back.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，吳武忠王楊行密薨，將佐共請宣諭使李儼承製授楊渥淮南節度使、東南諸道行營都統，兼侍中、弘農郡王。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Prince Wu Zhong of Wu Yang Xingmi died; generals and aides together requested that announcement envoy Li Yan, acting on imperial commission, invest Yang Wo as military governor of Huainan, commander-in-chief of the Southeast circuits' field camp, concurrently Grand Secretary, and Prince of Hongnong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Prince Wu Zhong of Wu, Yang Xingmi, died. His generals and aides jointly asked announcement envoy Li Yan to invest Yang Wo, under imperial commission, as military governor of Huainan, commander-in-chief of the Southeast circuits' field camp, concurrently Grand Secretary, and Prince of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 柳璨、蔣玄暉等議加朱全忠九錫，朝士多竊懷憤邑，禮部尚書蘇循獨揚言曰：「梁王功業顯大，歷數有歸，朝廷速宜揖讓。

translations.literal: Liu Can, Jiang Xuanhui, and others debated granting Zhu Quanzhong the Nine Bestowals; many court officials secretly harbored indignation, but Minister of Rites Su Xun alone proclaimed publicly: "The Liang Prince's achievements are great and manifest; the cycle of mandate has its destination—the court should quickly yield by bowing."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can, Jiang Xuanhui, and others debated granting Zhu Quanzhong the Nine Bestowals. Many court officials seethed in private, but Minister of Rites Su Xun alone declared openly, "The Prince of Liang's achievements are immense and the mandate clearly rests with him. The court should abdicate at once."

sentences.zh: 」朝士無敢違者。

translations.literal: " No court official dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: " No one in court dared dissent.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以全忠為相國，總百揆。

translations.literal: On xinsi, Quanzhong was made Chancellor of State, overseeing all affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Quanzhong was appointed Chancellor of State with authority over all government affairs.

sentences.zh: 以宣武、宣義、天平、護國、天雄、武順、佑國、河陽、義武、昭義、保義、戎昭、武定、泰寧、平廬、忠武、匡國、鎮國、武寧、忠義、荊南等二十一道為魏國，進封魏王，仍加九錫。

translations.literal: The twenty-one circuits of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, Huguo, Tianxiong, Wushun, Youguo, Heyang, Yiwu, Zhaoyi, Baoyi, Rongzhao, Wuding, Taining, Pinglu, Zhongwu, Kuangguo, Zhenguo, Wuning, Zhongyi, and Jingnan were made the State of Wei; he was advanced to Prince of Wei and still granted the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-one circuits of Xuanwu, Xuanyi, Tianping, Huguo, Tianxiong, Wushun, Youguo, Heyang, Yiwu, Zhaoyi, Baoyi, Rongzhao, Wuding, Taining, Pinglu, Zhongwu, Kuangguo, Zhenguo, Wuning, Zhongyi, and Jingnan were constituted as the State of Wei. Quanzhong was elevated to Prince of Wei and granted the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 全忠怒其稽緩，讓不受。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was angry at the delay and declined on pretext of yielding, refusing to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong, still angry at the delay, refused on pretext of modesty.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊子，命樞密使蔣玄暉繼手詔詣全忠諭指。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on wuzi, Commissioner of the Secretariat Jiang Xuanhui was ordered to follow with a hand edict going to Quanzhong to explain the intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wuzi, Commissioner of the Secretariat Jiang Xuanhui was sent with a handwritten edict to explain the emperor's intent to Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，玄暉自大梁還，言全忠怒不解。

translations.literal: On guisi, Xuanhui returned from Daliang and reported that Quanzhong's anger was not resolved.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Xuanhui returned from Daliang and reported that Quanzhong's rage had not subsided.

sentences.zh: 甲午，柳璨奏稱：「人望歸梁王，陛下釋重負，今其時也。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Liu Can memorialized: "The people's hopes return to the Liang Prince; Your Majesty may cast off the heavy burden—now is the time."
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Liu Can memorialized, "The people's hopes rest with the Prince of Liang. Your Majesty may lay down your heavy burden—the time has come."

sentences.zh: 」即日遣璨詣大梁達傳禪之意，全忠拒之。

translations.literal: " That same day Can was sent to Daliang to convey the intention of transferring the throne; Quanzhong refused it.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day Can was dispatched to Daliang to broach abdication. Quanzhong refused.

sentences.zh: 初，璨陷害朝士過多，全忠亦惡之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Can had framed too many court officials; Quanzhong also loathed him.
translations.idiomatic: Can had already framed too many court officials, and Quanzhong had come to despise him.

sentences.zh: 璨與蔣玄暉、張廷范朝夕宴聚，深相結，為全忠謀禪代事。

translations.literal: Can with Jiang Xuanhui and Zhang Tingfan feasted together morning and evening, bound themselves deeply, and plotted the matter of transfer and replacement for Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Can, Jiang Xuanhui, and Zhang Tingfan feasted together day and night, bound themselves closely, and schemed over Quanzhong's succession.

sentences.zh: 何太后泣遣宮人阿秋、阿虔達意玄暉，語以他日傳禪之後，求子母生全。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager He weeping sent palace women A-Qiu and A-Qian to convey her intent to Xuanhui, asking that after the day of throne transfer mother and son might be spared alive.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager He wept and sent palace women A-Qiu and A-Qian to Xuanhui, begging that after the abdication she and her son might be allowed to live.

sentences.zh: 王殷、趙殷衡譖玄暉，云「與柳璨、張廷范於積善宮夜宴，對太后焚香為誓，期興復唐祚。

translations.literal: Wang Yin and Zhao Yinheng slandered Xuanhui, saying: "With Liu Can and Zhang Tingfan he held a night feast at Jishan Palace, burned incense before the Empress Dowager as oath, and pledged to restore Tang's fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin and Zhao Yinheng slandered Xuanhui, claiming that "he banqueted at night in Jishan Palace with Liu Can and Zhang Tingfan, burned incense before the Empress Dowager as an oath, and pledged to restore the Tang dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」全忠信之，乙未，收玄暉及豐德庫使應頊、御廚使朱建武系河南獄；

translations.literal: " Quanzhong believed it; on yimwei, Xuanhui and Fengde Storehouse commissioner Ying Qi and Imperial Kitchen commissioner Zhu Jianwu were seized and imprisoned in Henan jail;
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong believed them. On yimwei, Xuanhui, Fengde Storehouse commissioner Ying Qi, and Imperial Kitchen commissioner Zhu Jianwu were arrested and jailed in Henan;

sentences.zh: 以王殷權知樞密，趙殷衡權判宣徽院事。

translations.literal: Wang Yin was made acting Commissioner of the Secretariat and Zhao Yinheng acting chief of the Palace Secretariat South Court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin was put in charge of the Secretariat on an acting basis, and Zhao Yinheng was given acting charge of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 全忠三表辭魏王、九錫之命。

translations.literal: Quanzhong three times submitted memorials declining the appointments as Prince of Wei and the Nine Bestowals.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong submitted three memorials declining the title of Prince of Wei and the Nine Bestowals.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔許之，更以為天下兵馬元帥，然全忠已修大梁府捨為宮闕矣。

translations.literal: On dingyou, an edict permitted it and again made him commander-in-chief of the world's armies and horses; yet Quanzhong had already renovated Daliang's government quarters into a palace.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, an edict granted his request and reappointed him commander-in-chief of all armies, though Quanzhong had already converted his Daliang headquarters into an imperial palace.

sentences.zh: 是日，斬蔣玄暉，杖殺應頊、朱建武。

translations.literal: That day Jiang Xuanhui was beheaded; Ying Qi and Zhu Jianwu were beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Jiang Xuanhui was beheaded, and Ying Qi and Zhu Jianwu were beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 庚子，省樞密使及宣徽南院使，獨置宣徽使一員，以王殷為之，趙殷衡為副使。

translations.literal: On gengzi, the Commissioner of the Secretariat and the Palace Secretariat South Court commissioner were abolished; only one Palace Secretariat commissioner was retained—Wang Yin was made it, and Zhao Yinheng deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the offices of Commissioner of the Secretariat and Palace Secretariat South Court commissioner were abolished. A single Palace Secretariat commissioner was retained: Wang Yin, with Zhao Yinheng as deputy.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，敕罷宮人宣傳詔命及參隨視朝。

translations.literal: On xinchou, an edict abolished palace women's announcing and transmitting edicts and attending and following court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, an edict barred palace women from proclaiming edicts and from attending court.

sentences.zh: 追削蔣玄暉為凶逆百姓，令河南揭屍於都門外，聚眾焚之。

translations.literal: Jiang Xuanhui was posthumously stripped to evil rebel commoner; Henan was ordered to expose the corpse outside the capital gate and gather the crowd to burn it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xuanhui was posthumously degraded to common rebel. Henan was ordered to display his corpse outside the capital gate and burn it before the assembled crowd.

sentences.zh: 玄暉既死，王殷、趙殷衡又誣玄暉私侍何太后，令阿秋、阿虔通導往來。

translations.literal: After Xuanhui's death, Wang Yin and Zhao Yinheng again falsely accused Xuanhui of privately attending Empress Dowager He and made A-Qiu and A-Qian go-between guides for coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanhui's death, Wang Yin and Zhao Yinheng further accused him of having secretly attended Empress Dowager He, with A-Qiu and A-Qian acting as go-betweens.

sentences.zh: 己酉，全忠密令殷、殷衡害太后於積善宮，敕追廢太后為庶人，阿秋、阿虔皆於殿前撲殺。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Quanzhong secretly ordered Yin and Yinheng to kill the Empress Dowager at Jishan Palace; an edict posthumously degraded the Empress Dowager to commoner; A-Qiu and A-Qian were both beaten to death before the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Quanzhong secretly ordered Yin and Yinheng to murder the Empress Dowager at Jishan Palace. An edict degraded her posthumously to commoner status, and A-Qiu and A-Qian were beaten to death in the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以皇太后喪，廢朝三日。

translations.literal: On gengxu, on account of the Empress Dowager's mourning, court audiences were suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, mourning for the Empress Dowager was observed with a three-day suspension of court audiences.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，敕以宮禁內亂，罷來年正月上辛謁郊廟禮。

translations.literal: On xinhai, an edict ordered that, due to disorder within the palace confines, the first month's upper xin day ceremony of worship at the suburban temples next year would be canceled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, an edict announced that due to turmoil within the palace, the first month's upper-xin ceremony of homage at the suburban temples would be canceled the following year.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，守司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事柳璨貶登州刺史，太常卿張廷范貶萊州司戶。

translations.literal: On guichou, Liu Can, acting Director of the Works, Grand Secretary of the Chancellery, and Associate Grand Councillor, was demoted to prefect of Deng Prefecture; Zhang Tingfan, Minister of Rites, was demoted to revenue clerk of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Liu Can—acting Director of the Works, Grand Secretary of the Chancellery, and Associate Grand Councillor—was demoted to prefect of Deng Prefecture, while Zhang Tingfan, Minister of Rites, was demoted to revenue clerk of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，斬璨於上東門外，車裂廷范於都市。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Can was beheaded outside the Upper East Gate; Tingfan was dismembered by chariots in the capital marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Liu Can was beheaded outside the Upper East Gate, and Zhang Tingfan was torn apart by chariots in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 璨臨刑呼曰：「負國賊柳璨，死其宜矣！

translations.literal: As Can faced execution he called out: "The treasonous minister Liu Can deserves to die!
translations.idiomatic: Facing execution, Liu Can cried out: "Liu Can, traitor to the state—death is what I deserve!

sentences.zh: 」西川將王宗朗不能守金州，焚其城邑，奔成都。

translations.literal: The Shu commander Wang Zonglang could not hold Jin Prefecture; he burned its towns and fled to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu commander Wang Zonglang, unable to hold Jin Prefecture, burned its towns and fled to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 戎昭節度使馮行襲復取金州，奏稱「金州荒殘，乞徙理均州，」從之。

translations.literal: Feng Xingxi, military governor of Rongzhao, recovered Jin Prefecture and memorialized saying, "Jin Prefecture is desolate and ruined; I beg to move the seat of administration to Jun Prefecture." The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingxi, military governor of Rongzhao, reconquered Jin Prefecture and memorialized that the prefecture was too devastated to serve as a seat of government, asking to relocate administration to Jun Prefecture. His request was approved.

sentences.zh: 更以行襲領武安軍。

translations.literal: Xingxi was further appointed to command the Wu'an army.
translations.idiomatic: Xingxi was additionally given command of the Wu'an army.

sentences.zh: 陳詢不能守睦州，奔於廣陵，淮南招討使陶雅入據其城。

translations.literal: Chen Xun could not hold Muzhou and fled to Guangling; Tao Ya, the Huainan pacification commissioner, entered and occupied its city.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xun, unable to hold Muzhou, fled to Guangling; Tao Ya, Huainan's pacification commissioner, entered the city and took possession of it.

sentences.zh: 楊渥之去宣州也，欲取其幄幕及親兵以行，觀察使王茂章不與，渥怒。

translations.literal: When Yang Wo was leaving Xuan Prefecture, he wished to take his tent equipage and personal troops with him; Wang Maozhang, the observation commissioner, would not grant it, and Wo grew angry.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Wo departed Xuan Prefecture, he wanted to take his tent equipage and personal troops with him. The observation commissioner Wang Maozhang refused, and Wo was enraged.

sentences.zh: 既襲位，遣馬步都指揮使李簡等將兵襲之。

translations.literal: After he succeeded to the position, he sent the infantry and cavalry commander Li Jian and others to lead troops in an attack upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had assumed leadership, he dispatched Li Jian, commander of infantry and cavalry, along with others to lead troops against Wang Maozhang.

sentences.zh: 湖南兵寇淮南，淮南牙內指揮使楊彪擊卻之。

translations.literal: Hunan troops raided Huainan; Yang Biao, the Huainan garrison commander, repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunan forces raided Huainan, Yang Biao, commander of the Huainan garrison troops, drove them back.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝下之下天祐三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial—Lower Part, Lower Section: Third Year of Tianyou (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial—Lower Part, Lower Section: Third Year of Tianyou (

sentences.zh: 丙寅，公元九零六年）

translations.literal: bingyin, 906 CE)
translations.idiomatic: bingyin, 906 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬戌，靈武節度使韓遜奏吐番七千餘騎營於宗高谷，將擊嗢末及取涼州。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on renxu, Han Xun, military governor of Lingwu, reported that more than seven thousand Tibetan cavalry were encamped at Zonggao Valley, intending to attack the Wamo and seize Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renxu, Han Xun, military governor of Lingwu, reported that over seven thousand Tibetan horsemen had encamped at Zonggao Valley with the intention of attacking the Wamo and capturing Liang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李簡兵奄至宣州，王茂章度不能守，帥眾奔兩浙。

translations.literal: Li Jian's troops suddenly arrived at Xuan Prefecture; Wang Maozhang judged he could not hold it and led his force to flee to the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian's army suddenly appeared at Xuan Prefecture. Judging the city indefensible, Wang Maozhang led his men in flight to the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 親兵上蔡刁彥能辭以母老，不從行，登城諭眾曰：「王府命我招諭汝曹，大兵行至矣。

translations.literal: The personal troops' Shangcai native Diao Yanneng pleaded that his mother was aged and did not follow on the march; he ascended the wall and addressed the multitude saying, "The princely residence has ordered me to summon and reassure you—all of you—the great army is already near."
translations.idiomatic: Diao Yanneng of Shangcai, a man of the personal guard, pleaded that his aged mother kept him from marching. He mounted the wall and proclaimed to the crowd: "The princely headquarters has charged me to summon and reassure you—the main army is already at hand."

sentences.zh: 」眾由是定。

translations.literal: The multitude was thereby settled.
translations.idiomatic: The people were thus calmed.

sentences.zh: 陶雅畏茂章斷其歸路，引兵還歙州，錢鏐復取睦州。

translations.literal: Tao Ya feared that Maozhang would cut off his route of return and withdrew his troops to She Prefecture; Qian Liu recovered Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Wang Maozhang would cut off his retreat, Tao Ya withdrew to She Prefecture, and Qian Liu retook Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 鏐以茂章為鎮東節度副使，更名景仁。

translations.literal: Liu appointed Maozhang deputy military governor of Zhendong and changed his name to Jingren.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu appointed Wang Maozhang deputy military governor of Zhendong and renamed him Jingren.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，加靜海節度使曲承裕同平章事。

translations.literal: On yichou, Qu Chengyu, military governor of Jinghai, was made Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Qu Chengyu, military governor of Jinghai, was appointed Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 初，田承嗣鎮魏博，選募六州驍勇之士五千人為牙軍，厚其給賜以自衛，為腹心。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Tian Chengsi governed Weibo, he selected and recruited five thousand fierce warriors from the six prefectures to form the garrison guard army, enriching their stipends and rewards for his own protection as his innermost force.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days, when Tian Chengsi held Weibo, he selected five thousand elite fighters from the six prefectures to form the garrison guard—the elite corps—and lavished pay and rewards upon them as his personal shield and innermost core.

sentences.zh: 自是父子相繼，親黨膠固，歲久益驕橫，小不如意，輒族舊帥而易之。

translations.literal: From then on they succeeded father to son; kinsmen and partisans bonded firmly; year after year they grew ever more arrogant and overbearing—whenever anything fell short of their wishes, they would execute the old commander by clan extermination and replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter leadership passed from father to son, kinsmen and allies entwined like glue. With the years they grew ever bolder, and at the slightest disappointment they would wipe out the ruling commander by clan extermination and install another.

sentences.zh: 自史憲誠以來皆立於其手。

translations.literal: From Shi Xiancheng onward, all were enthroned at their hands.
translations.idiomatic: From Shi Xiancheng onward, every commander had been installed at their pleasure.

sentences.zh: 天雄節度使羅紹威心惡之，力不能制。

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei, military governor of Tianxiong, hated them in his heart but lacked the strength to control them.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei, military governor of Tianxiong, loathed them but was powerless to restrain them.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠之圍鳳翔也，紹威遣軍將楊利言密以情告全忠，欲借其兵以誅之。

translations.literal: When Zhu Quanzhong was besieging Fengxiang, Shaowei sent the army commander Yang Liyan secretly to report his situation to Quanzhong, wishing to borrow his troops to exterminate them.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhu Quanzhong was besieging Fengxiang, Shaowei sent his officer Yang Liyan to confide in Quanzhong in secret, hoping to borrow Quanzhong's forces to destroy the guard corps.

sentences.zh: 全忠以事方急，未暇如其請，陰許之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong, as affairs were pressing, had no leisure to accede to his request but secretly assented.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong, pressed by urgent affairs, could not act on the request at once but gave his secret consent.

sentences.zh: 及李公佺作亂，紹威益懼，復遣牙將臧延范趣全忠。

translations.literal: When Li Gongxian raised rebellion, Shaowei grew even more fearful and again sent the garrison officer Zang Yanfan to urge Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gongxian rebelled, Shaowei's fear deepened, and he again dispatched the guard officer Zang Yanfan to press Quanzhong for action.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃發河南諸鎮兵七萬，遣其將李思安將之，會魏、鎮兵屯深州樂城，聲言擊滄州，討其納李公佺也。

translations.literal: Quanzhong thereupon mobilized seventy thousand troops from the various prefectures of Henan, sent his commander Li Si'an to lead them, and joined with Wei and Zhen troops to encamp at Lecheng in Shen Prefecture, publicly announcing an attack on Cangzhou to punish its harboring of Li Gongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then mustered seventy thousand troops from the Henan prefectures, placed them under his general Li Si'an, and joined Wei and Zhen forces at Lecheng in Shen Prefecture, proclaiming an expedition against Cangzhou to punish its sheltering of Li Gongxian.

sentences.zh: 會全忠女適紹威子廷規者卒，全忠遣客將馬嗣勳實甲兵於橐中，選長直兵千人為擔夫，帥之入魏，詐雲會葬，全忠自以大軍繼其後，雲赴行營，牙軍皆不之疑。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong's daughter, who had married Shaowei's son Tinggui, died, Quanzhong sent the retainer general Ma Sixun with armor and weapons packed in chests, selected a thousand long-service troops as bearers, and led them into Wei, falsely claiming to attend the funeral; Quanzhong himself followed with a large army, claiming to proceed to the field camp—the garrison guard army never suspected them.
translations.idiomatic: When the daughter Quanzhong had married to Shaowei's son Tinggui died, Quanzhong sent his retainer-commander Ma Sixun with armor hidden in traveling chests, chose a thousand veteran troops disguised as porters, and marched them into Wei under the pretense of attending the funeral. Quanzhong himself followed at the head of a great army, claiming he was bound for the field camp—and the garrison guard never suspected a thing.

sentences.zh: 庚午，紹威潛遣人入庫斷弓弦、甲襻。

translations.literal: On gengwu, Shaowei secretly sent men into the stores to cut bowstrings and armor lacings.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Shaowei secretly sent men into the arsenals to sever bowstrings and armor lacings.

sentences.zh: 是夕，紹威帥其奴客數百，與嗣勳合擊牙軍。

translations.literal: That evening, Shaowei led several hundred of his household retainers and joined with Sixun in a combined assault on the garrison guard.
translations.idiomatic: That night, Shaowei led several hundred household warriors and joined Sixun in a surprise attack on the guard corps.

sentences.zh: 牙軍欲戰而弓甲皆不可用，遂闔營殪之，凡八千家，嬰孺無遺。

translations.literal: The guard army wished to fight but bows and armor were all unusable; the entire camp was thus annihilated—eight thousand households in all, infants and children none spared.
translations.idiomatic: The guard tried to fight, but their bows and armor had been rendered useless. The entire camp was slaughtered—eight thousand households in all, down to the last infant.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，全忠引兵入城。

translations.literal: At dawn, Quanzhong led his troops into the city.
translations.idiomatic: At first light, Quanzhong marched his army into the city.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以權知寧遠留後龐巨昭、嶺南西道留後葉廣略並為節度使。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Pang Juzhao, acting military governor of Ningyuan, and Ye Guanglue, acting military governor of Lingnan West Circuit, were both made full military governors.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Pang Juzhao, provisional commander of Ningyuan, and Ye Guanglue, provisional commander of Lingnan West Circuit, were both confirmed as full military governors.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，錢鏐如睦州。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Qian Liu went to Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Qian Liu traveled to Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 西川將王宗阮攻歸州，獲其將韓從實。

translations.literal: The Shu commander Wang Zongruan attacked Guizhou and captured its commander Han Congshi.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu general Wang Zongruan attacked Guizhou and captured the enemy commander Han Congshi.

sentences.zh: 陳璋聞陶雅歸歙，自婺州退保衢州。

translations.literal: When Chen Zhang heard that Tao Ya had returned to She, he withdrew from Wuzhou to hold Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Tao Ya had returned to She Prefecture, Chen Zhang withdrew from Wuzhou and fell back to defend Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兩浙將方永珍等取婺州，進攻衢州。

translations.literal: The Two Zhes commanders Fang Yongzhen and others took Wuzhou and advanced to attack Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yongzhen and other Two Zhes generals captured Wuzhou and pressed on to attack Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 楊渥遣先鋒指揮使陳知新攻湖南。

translations.literal: Yang Wo sent the vanguard commander Chen Zhixin to attack Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wo dispatched Chen Zhixin, commander of the vanguard, to attack Hunan.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙丑，知新拔岳州，逐刺史許德勳，渥以知新為岳州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third month, on yichou, Zhixin captured Yue Prefecture, expelled the prefect Xu Dexun, and Wo appointed Zhixin prefect of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yichou, Chen Zhixin took Yue Prefecture, drove out the prefect Xu Dexun, and Yang Wo appointed him prefect of Yue.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以朱全忠為鹽鐵、度支、戶部三司都制置使。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Zhu Quanzhong was made chief commissioner for the overall administration of the three bureaus of Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Zhu Quanzhong was appointed chief commissioner of the three revenue bureaus—Salt and Iron, Revenue, and Public Works.

sentences.zh: 三司之名始於此。

translations.literal: The name "Three Bureaus" begins from this.
translations.idiomatic: The title "Three Bureaus" dates from this appointment.

sentences.zh: 全忠辭不受。

translations.literal: Quanzhong declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day guimo, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day (guiwei), a solar eclipse occurred.

sentences.zh: 羅紹威既誅牙軍，魏之諸軍皆懼，紹威雖數撫諭之，而猜怨益甚。

translations.literal: After Luo Shaowei had exterminated the guard army, all the armies of Wei were fearful; though Shaowei repeatedly soothed and reassured them, suspicion and resentment grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: After Luo Shaowei destroyed the guard corps, every Wei army was seized with fear. Though Shaowei offered repeated reassurances, suspicion and resentment only deepened.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠營於魏州城東數旬，將北巡行營，會天雄牙將史仁遇作亂，聚眾數萬據高唐，自稱留後，天雄巡內州縣多應之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong encamped east of Weizhou city for several weeks and was about to tour the northern field camps when Tianxiong guard officer Shi Renyu raised rebellion, gathering a host of tens of thousands to hold Gaotang, declaring himself acting military governor; many counties within the Tianxiong circuit responded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong had encamped east of Weizhou for several weeks and was preparing to inspect the northern field camps when Tianxiong guard officer Shi Renyu rebelled. Renyu rallied tens of thousands of men, seized Gaotang, and declared himself acting military governor—and counties throughout the Tianxiong circuit rose in response.

sentences.zh: 全忠移軍入城，遣使召行營兵還攻高唐，至歷亭，魏兵在行營者作亂，與仁遇相應。

translations.literal: Quanzhong moved his army into the city and sent envoys summoning field-camp troops back to attack Gaotang; at Liting, Wei troops in the field camps mutinied and coordinated with Renyu.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong moved his army into the city and sent orders recalling field troops to attack Gaotang. At Liting, Wei soldiers in the camps mutinied in concert with Renyu.

sentences.zh: 元帥府左司馬李周彝、右司馬苻道昭擊之，所殺殆半，進攻高唐，克之，城中兵民無少長皆死。

translations.literal: Left Chief of Staff Li Zhouyi and Right Chief of Staff Fu Daozhao of the marshal's headquarters attacked them, killing nearly half; they advanced to attack Gaotang, captured it, and within the city soldiers and civilians, young and old alike, were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhouyi, left chief of staff, and Fu Daozhao, right chief of staff, at the marshal's headquarters struck back, killing nearly half the rebels. They advanced on Gaotang, took the city, and put every soul within it to the sword—soldiers and civilians, young and old alike.

sentences.zh: 擒史仁遇，鋸殺之。

translations.literal: Shi Renyu was captured and sawed to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Renyu was captured and executed by sawing.

sentences.zh: 先是，仁遇求救於河東及滄州，李克用遣其將李嗣昭將三千騎攻邢州以救之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Renyu had sought rescue from Hedong and Cangzhou; Li Keyong sent his commander Li Sizhao to lead three thousand cavalry in an attack on Xing Prefecture to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Renyu had appealed for aid to Hedong and Cangzhou. Li Keyong dispatched Li Sizhao with three thousand horsemen to attack Xing Prefecture in relief.

sentences.zh: 時邢州兵才二百，團練使牛存節守之，嗣昭攻七日不克。

translations.literal: At the time Xing Prefecture had only two hundred troops; Niu Cunjie, the militia commissioner, held it; Sizhao assaulted for seven days without success.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Prefecture had only two hundred defenders under the militia commissioner Niu Cunjie. Sizhao besieged it for seven days without success.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣右長直都將張筠將數千騎助存節守城，筠伏兵於馬嶺，擊嗣昭，敗之，嗣昭遁去。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent the right long-service commander Zhang Yun to lead several thousand cavalry to help Cunjie defend the city; Yun ambushed troops at Maling, struck Sizhao, defeated him, and Sizhao fled.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Zhang Yun, right commander of the long-service corps, with several thousand cavalry to reinforce Cunjie. Yun lay in ambush at Maling, struck Sizhao, routed him, and Sizhao fled.

sentences.zh: 義昌節度使劉守文遣兵萬人攻貝州，又攻冀州，拔蓨縣，進攻阜城。

translations.literal: Liu Shouwen, military governor of Yichang, sent ten thousand troops to attack Bei Prefecture; he also attacked Ji Prefecture, captured Tiao County, and advanced to attack Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouwen, military governor of Yichang, dispatched ten thousand men against Bei Prefecture, then turned on Ji Prefecture, captured Tiao County, and pressed on toward Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 時鎮州大將王釗攻魏州叛將李重霸於宗城。

translations.literal: At the time the Zhen Prefecture great general Wang Zhao was attacking the Wei rebel commander Li Chongba at Zongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Zhao, a senior general of Zhen Prefecture, was besieging the Wei rebel Li Chongba at Zongcheng.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣歸救冀州，滄州兵去。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent him to return and rescue Ji Prefecture, and the Cangzhou troops departed.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong ordered him to break off and save Ji Prefecture, and the Cangzhou army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丙午，重霸棄城走，汴將胡規追斬之。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Chongba abandoned the city and fled; the Bian commander Hu Gui pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Li Chongba abandoned the city and fled; the Bian general Hu Gui pursued and killed him.

sentences.zh: 鎮南節度使鍾傳以養子延規為江州刺史。

translations.literal: Zhong Chuan, military governor of Zhennan, appointed his adopted son Yangui prefect of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Chuan, military governor of Zhennan, appointed his adopted son Yan Gui prefect of Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 傳薨，軍中立其子匡時為留後。

translations.literal: When Chuan died, the army enthroned his son Kuangshi as acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong Chuan died, the army installed his son Kuangshi as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 延規恨不得立，遣使降淮南。

translations.literal: Yangui resented that he had not been enthroned and sent envoys to surrender to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gui, bitter over being passed over, sent envoys offering surrender to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁巳，朱全忠如洺州，遂巡北邊，視戎備，還，入於魏。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on dingsi, Zhu Quanzhong went to Ming Prefecture, then toured the northern frontier to inspect military preparedness; returning, he entered Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on dingsi, Zhu Quanzhong proceeded to Ming Prefecture, made a circuit of the northern frontier to inspect defenses, then returned and entered Wei.

sentences.zh: 丙子，廢戎昭軍，並均、房隸忠義軍。

translations.literal: On bingzi, the Rongzhao army was abolished; Jun and Fang prefectures were both placed under the Zhongyi army.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, the Rongzhao command was abolished, and Jun and Fang prefectures were annexed to the Zhongyi command.

sentences.zh: 以武定節度使馮行襲為匡國節度使。

translations.literal: Feng Xingxi, military governor of Wuding, was made military governor of Kuangguo.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Xingxi, military governor of Wuding, was appointed military governor of Kuangguo.

sentences.zh: 楊渥以升州刺史秦裴為西南行營都招討使，將兵擊鍾匡時於江西。

translations.literal: Yang Wo appointed Qin Pei, prefect of Sheng Prefecture, chief pacification commissioner of the southwestern field army and sent troops to attack Zhong Kuangshi in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wo appointed Qin Pei, prefect of Sheng Prefecture, chief pacification commissioner of the southwestern field army, and sent him to attack Zhong Kuangshi in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲申，復以忠義軍為山南東道。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on jiashen, the Zhongyi army was again made Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiashen, the Zhongyi command was restored to its former name, Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠以長安鄰於邠、岐，數有戰爭，奏徙佑國節度使韓建於淄青，以淄青節度使長社王重師為佑國節度使。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong, because Chang'an bordered Bin and Qi and fighting repeatedly occurred, memorialized to transfer Han Jian, military governor of Youguo, to Ziqing, and to make Wang Chongshi of Changshe, military governor of Ziqing, military governor of Youguo.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chang'an lay adjacent to Bin and Qi and saw frequent warfare, Zhu Quanzhong memorialized to transfer Han Jian from Youguo to Ziqing and appoint Wang Chongshi of Changshe, the Ziqing military governor, as military governor of Youguo in his stead.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，朱全忠克相州。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhu Quanzhong captured Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Zhu Quanzhong took Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時魏之亂兵散據貝、博、澶、相、衛州及魏之諸縣，全忠分命諸將攻討，至是悉平之，引兵南還。

translations.literal: At the time Wei's mutinous troops were scattered holding Bei, Bo, Chan, Xiang, and Wei prefectures and the various counties of Wei; Quanzhong dispatched various commanders to attack and suppress them; by this time all were pacified, and he led his troops south in return.
translations.idiomatic: Wei mutineers still held scattered positions across Bei, Bo, Chan, Xiang, and Wei prefectures and throughout Wei's counties. Quanzhong dispatched his generals to suppress them one by one, and by this time all had been subdued. He then marched his army southward.

sentences.zh: 全忠留魏半歲，羅紹威供億，所殺牛羊豕近七十萬，資糧稱是，所賂遺又近百萬，比去，蓄積為之一空。

translations.literal: Quanzhong had remained in Wei half a year; Luo Shaowei provisioned the host—cattle, sheep, and swine slaughtered approached seven hundred thousand; provisions and grain were comparable; gifts and presents also approached one million; by the time he left, accumulated stores were emptied thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong had lingered in Wei for half a year. Luo Shaowei fed his army, slaughtering nearly seven hundred thousand head of cattle, sheep, and swine, with provisions to match, and lavished nearly a million more in gifts. By the time Quanzhong departed, Wei's accumulated stores had been utterly drained.

sentences.zh: 紹威雖去其逼，而魏兵自是衰弱。

translations.literal: Though Shaowei had removed their pressure, from this the Wei troops were weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei had rid himself of the guard corps' stranglehold, but Wei's military strength was thereafter permanently diminished.

sentences.zh: 紹威悔之，謂人曰：「合六州四十三縣鐵，不能為此錯也！

translations.literal: Shaowei regretted it and said to others: "If all the iron of the six prefectures and forty-three counties were forged together, it could not make up for this blunder!"
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei came to rue his decision. "If all the iron of six prefectures and forty-three counties were smelted into one," he told others, "it could not atone for this mistake!"

sentences.zh: 」壬申，全忠至大梁。

translations.literal: On renshen, Quanzhong reached Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Quanzhong arrived at Daliang.

sentences.zh: 秦裴至洪州，軍於蓼州。

translations.literal: Qin Pei reached Hong Prefecture and encamped at Liao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Pei reached Hong Prefecture and made camp at Liao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 諸將請阻水立寨，裴不從。

translations.literal: The commanders requested to block the water and establish a stockade; Pei did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged him to dam the water and build a fortified camp; Pei refused.

sentences.zh: 鍾匡時果遣其將劉楚據之。

translations.literal: Zhong Kuangshi indeed sent his commander Liu Chu to seize and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Kuangshi duly sent his general Liu Chu to occupy the position.

sentences.zh: 諸將以咎裴，裴曰：「匡時驍將獨楚一人耳，若帥眾守城，不可猝拔，吾故以要害誘致之耳。

translations.literal: The commanders blamed Pei; Pei said: "Among Kuangshi's fierce commanders Chu alone stands out; if he led the multitude to defend the city, it could not be taken suddenly—I therefore lured him to this critical point."
translations.idiomatic: The officers reproached Pei, but he replied: "Of Kuangshi's able generals, only Liu Chu is truly formidable. Had Chu held the city with a full garrison, we could never have taken it quickly. That is why I baited him to this critical spot."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，裴破寨，執楚，遂圍洪州，饒州刺史唐寶請降。

translations.literal: Before long, Pei broke the stockade, captured Chu, then besieged Hong Prefecture; Tang Bao, prefect of Rao Prefecture, requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Pei stormed the camp, captured Liu Chu, and laid siege to Hong Prefecture. Tang Bao, prefect of Rao, offered his surrender.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙酉，李茂貞遣其子侃為質於西川，王建以侃知彭州。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yiyou, Li Maozhen sent his son Kan as hostage to Shu; Wang Jian made Kan administrator of Peng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yiyou, Li Maozhen sent his son Kan as a hostage to Shu, and Wang Jian appointed him administrator of Peng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠以幽、滄相首尾為魏患，欲先取滄州，甲辰，引兵發大梁。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong, because You and Cang mutually supported each other as a Wei threat, wished first to take Cangzhou; on jiachen, he led troops departing from Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong, judging You and Cang a joint threat to Wei through their mutual support, resolved to take Cangzhou first. On jiachen he led his army out of Daliang.

sentences.zh: 兩浙兵圍衢州，衢州刺史陳璋告急於淮南。

translations.literal: Two Zhes troops besieged Qu Prefecture; Chen Zhang, prefect of Qu Prefecture, reported urgency to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Two Zhes forces besieged Qu Prefecture, and the prefect Chen Zhang sent desperate appeals to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 楊渥遣左廂馬步都虞候周本將兵迎璋。

translations.literal: Yang Wo sent the left wing cavalry and infantry inspector Zhou Ben to lead troops to welcome Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wo dispatched Zhou Ben, inspector of the left wing cavalry and infantry, to lead troops to Chen Zhang's relief.

sentences.zh: 本至衢州，浙人解圍，陳於城下。

translations.literal: Ben reached Qu Prefecture; the Zhe troops lifted the siege and drew up in formation below the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When Ben reached Qu Prefecture, the Zhe army lifted the siege and drew up in battle order below the walls.

sentences.zh: 璋帥眾歸於本，兩浙兵取衢州。

translations.literal: Zhang led his multitude over to Ben; the Two Zhes troops took Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhang led his forces over to Zhou Ben, and the Two Zhes army took possession of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 呂師造曰：「浙人近我而不動，輕我也，請擊之！

translations.literal: Lu Shizao said: "The Zhe men are near us yet do not move—they hold us in contempt; I request we strike them!"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shizao urged: "The Zhe troops are right beside us and yet hold still—they are treating us with contempt. I beg leave to attack!"

sentences.zh: 」本曰：「吾受命迎陳使君，今至矣，何為復戰！

translations.literal: Ben said: "I received orders to welcome Commissioner Chen; now that he has arrived, why fight again!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ben replied: "My orders were to escort Commissioner Chen. He is here now—why should we fight again?"

sentences.zh: 彼必有以待我也。

translations.literal: They surely have preparations awaiting us.
translations.idiomatic: Surely they have some stratagem waiting for us.

sentences.zh: 」遂引兵還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the troops back.
translations.idiomatic: He then withdrew his troops.

sentences.zh: 本為之殿，浙人躡之，本中道設伏，大破之。

translations.literal: Ben served as rearguard for them; the Zhe men pursued close behind; Ben ambushed midway and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Ben himself covered the retreat. When the Zhe army pressed close in pursuit, he laid an ambush along the way and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛亥朔，朱全忠自白馬渡河，丁卯，至滄州，軍於長蘆，滄人不出。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the first day xinhai, Zhu Quanzhong crossed the river from Baima; on dingmao, he reached Cangzhou and encamped at Changlu; the men of Cang did not sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day (xinhai), Zhu Quanzhong crossed the Yellow River at Baima. On dingmao he reached Cangzhou and encamped at Changlu; the defenders of Cangzhou refused to come out.

sentences.zh: 羅紹威饋運，自魏至長蘆五百里，不絕於路。

translations.literal: Luo Shaowei sent provisions continuously; from Wei to Changlu five hundred li, without interruption along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shaowei maintained an unbroken supply line from Wei to Changlu—five hundred li of ceaseless convoys.

sentences.zh: 又建元帥府捨於魏，所過驛亭供酒饌、幄幕、什器，上下數十萬人，無一不備。

translations.literal: He also built a marshal's headquarters compound at Wei; at every post station along the route he supplied wine and food, tent equipage, and utensils—for the host above and below numbering several hundred thousand, nothing was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: He also erected a marshal's headquarters at Wei and at every relay station along the route furnished wine, food, tents, and equipment—nothing omitted for an army of hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 秦裴拔洪州，虜鍾匡時等五千人以歸。

translations.literal: Qin Pei captured Hong Prefecture, took captive Zhong Kuangshi and others—five thousand men—and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Pei captured Hong Prefecture, taking Zhong Kuangshi and some five thousand captives back with him.

sentences.zh: 楊渥自兼鎮南節度使，以裴為洪州制置使。

translations.literal: Yang Wo himself concurrently assumed the post of military governor of Zhennan and appointed Pei commissioner for the administration of Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wo assumed the post of Zhennan military governor himself and appointed Qin Pei commissioner for the administration of Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 靜難節度使楊崇本以鳳翔、保塞、彰義、保義之兵攻夏州，匡國節度使劉知俊邀擊坊州之兵，斬首三千餘級，擒坊州刺史劉彥暉。

translations.literal: Yang Chongben, military governor of Jingnan, led troops from Fengxiang, Baosai, Zhangyi, and Baoyi to attack Xia Prefecture; Liu Zhijun, military governor of Kuangguo, intercepted and struck the Feng Prefecture troops, beheading more than three thousand; he captured Liu Yanhui, prefect of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chongben, military governor of Jingnan, led armies from Fengxiang, Baosai, Zhangyi, and Baoyi against Xia Prefecture. Liu Zhijun, military governor of Kuangguo, intercepted the Feng Prefecture contingent, took more than three thousand heads, and captured Liu Yanhui, prefect of Feng.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭救滄州，戰屢敗。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong came to rescue Cangzhou and was repeatedly defeated in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong marched to relieve Cangzhou but suffered defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 乃下令境內：「男子十五以上，七十以下，悉自備兵糧詣行營，軍發之後，有一人在閭裡，刑無赦！

translations.literal: He thereupon issued an order within his territory: "Men from fifteen upward and below seventy shall all equip themselves with weapons and provisions and proceed to the field camp; after the army has marched, if a single person remains in the hamlets, punishment without pardon!"
translations.idiomatic: He then issued orders throughout his domain: "Every man from fifteen to seventy shall equip himself with arms and rations and report to the field camp. After the army marches, any man found still at home in the villages shall be punished without mercy!"

sentences.zh: 」或諫曰：「今老弱悉行，婦人不能轉餉，此令必行，濫刑者眾矣！

translations.literal: Someone remonstrated saying: "Now with old and weak all marching forth, women cannot transport provisions—if this order must be enforced, those punished by excessive sentencing will be many!"
translations.idiomatic: An adviser objected: "If the old and weak all march away, women will be unable to haul supplies. Enforce this order and the ranks of those punished will swell beyond measure!"

sentences.zh: 」乃命勝執兵者盡行，文其面曰「定霸都」，士人則文其腕或臂曰「一心事主」，於是境內士民，稚孺之外無不文者。

translations.literal: He then ordered that all able to bear arms should march forth; their faces were tattooed with the words "Ding Ba Capital"; scholars had their wrists or arms tattooed with the words "Wholeheartedly serving the lord"—thus within the territory, among gentry and commoners, apart from infants none went unmarked.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered every able-bodied man to march, tattooing their faces with "Ding Ba Capital" and marking scholars on wrist or arm with "Wholeheartedly serving the lord." Throughout his domain, not a soul above infancy was left unmarked.

sentences.zh: 得兵十萬，軍於瓦橋。

translations.literal: He obtained one hundred thousand troops and encamped at Waqiao.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered one hundred thousand troops and encamped at Waqiao.

sentences.zh: 時汴軍築壘圍滄州，鳥鼠不能通。

translations.literal: At the time the Bian army was building ramparts besieging Cangzhou; birds and mice could not pass through.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Bian army had ringed Cangzhou with siege works so tight that not even birds or mice could slip through.

sentences.zh: 仁恭畏其強，不敢戰。

translations.literal: Rengong feared their strength and dared not give battle.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong feared their strength and dared not give battle.

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，丸土而食，或互相掠啖。

translations.literal: Food in the city was exhausted; they rolled earth into balls to eat, and some preyed on one another and devoured each other.
translations.idiomatic: When food in the city ran out, the people ate balls of earth; some turned to cannibalism.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠使人說劉守文曰：「援兵勢不相及，何不早降！

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent someone to persuade Liu Shouwen, saying: "Relief troops cannot reach you in time—why not surrender early!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent an envoy to persuade Liu Shouwen, saying, "Relief cannot reach you in time—why not surrender now?"

sentences.zh: 」守文登城應之曰：「僕於幽州，父子也。

translations.literal: " Shouwen mounted the wall and answered: "I and Youzhou are father and son."
translations.idiomatic: " Shouwen mounted the wall and replied, "I and Youzhou are father and son."

sentences.zh: 梁王方以大義服天下，若子叛父而來，將安用之！

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang is just now winning the realm by great righteousness—if a son rebels against his father and comes to you, how could you employ him!
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang wins the realm through righteousness—if a son betrays his father and comes to you, how could you accept him!

sentences.zh: 」全忠愧其辭直，為之緩攻。

translations.literal: " Quanzhong was ashamed at his blunt words and slackened the assault on his account.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong was shamed by his blunt reply and eased the assault on his account.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙戌，王建始立行台於蜀，建東向舞蹈，號慟，稱「自大駕東遷，制命不通，請權立行台，用李晟、鄭畋故事，承製封拜。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingxu, Wang Jian first established a provisional government office in Shu; Jian danced facing east, wailed aloud, and declared: "Since the imperial carriage moved east, imperial orders no longer reach us—I request permission to establish a provisional office provisionally, following the precedents of Li Sheng and Zheng Tian, to receive imperial commissions and grant titles and appointments."
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingxu, Wang Jian established a provisional government office in Shu. He danced facing east, wailed aloud, and declared, "Since the emperor was taken east, imperial orders no longer reach us. I ask leave to establish a provisional office, following the precedents of Li Sheng and Zheng Tian, to receive imperial commissions and grant titles and appointments."

sentences.zh: 」仍以膀帖告諭所部籓鎮州縣。

translations.literal: " He also used posted notices to announce and instruct the military governors, prefectures, and counties under his authority.
translations.idiomatic: " He also posted notices to announce this to the governors, prefectures, and counties under his authority.

sentences.zh: 劉仁恭求救於河東，前後百餘輩。

translations.literal: Liu Rengong appealed for aid to Hedong more than a hundred times in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengong sent more than a hundred successive appeals for aid to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 李克用恨仁恭返覆，竟未之許，其子存勖諫曰：「今天下之勢，歸朱溫者什七八，雖強大如魏博、鎮、定，莫不附之。

translations.literal: Li Keyong resented Rengong's fickleness and in the end did not consent; his son Cunxu remonstrated, saying: "Today's situation in the realm—seven or eight tenths have gone to Zhu Wen; even powers as great as Weibo, Zhen, and Ding all attach themselves to him."
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong resented Rengong's fickleness and refused; his son Cunxu remonstrated, saying, "Seven or eight tenths of the realm now belong to Zhu Wen—even powers as great as Weibo, Zhen, and Ding have submitted to him."

sentences.zh: 自河以北，能為溫患者獨我與幽、滄耳，今幽、滄為溫所困，我不與之並力拒之，非我之利也。

translations.literal: North of the Yellow River, only we and You and Cang can still harm Wen; now You and Cang are beset by Wen—if we do not join forces to resist together, it is not to our advantage.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yellow River, only we and Youzhou and Cangzhou can still threaten Wen. Now they are besieged—if we do not join them, we harm ourselves.

sentences.zh: 夫為天下者不顧小怨，且彼嘗困我而我救其急，以德懷之，乃一舉而名實附也。

translations.literal: One who holds the realm does not heed small grievances; moreover, they once beset us while we now relieve their extremity—win them by virtue, and in one stroke both name and substance will attach to us.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler of the realm does not nurse petty grudges. They once beset us; if we now save them in their extremity and win them with virtue, we gain both reputation and power in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 此乃吾復振之時，不可失也。

translations.literal: This is our moment to revive our fortunes—we must not let it slip.
translations.idiomatic: This is our chance to revive our fortunes—we must not miss it.

sentences.zh: 」克用以為然，與將佐謀召幽州兵與攻潞州，曰：「於彼可以解圍，於我可以拓境。

translations.literal: " Keyong thought this right and discussed with his generals and staff summoning Youzhou troops to attack Luzhou jointly, saying: "For them it can lift the siege; for us it can extend our territory."
translations.idiomatic: " Keyong agreed and discussed with his officers summoning Youzhou troops to attack Luzhou, saying, "For them it lifts the siege; for us it extends our territory."

sentences.zh: 」乃許仁恭和，召其兵。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he granted Rengong peace and summoned his troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He then made peace with Rengong and summoned his troops.

sentences.zh: 仁恭遣都指揮使李溥將兵三萬詣晉陽，克用遣其將周德威、李嗣昭將兵與之共攻潞州。

translations.literal: Rengong dispatched the chief commander Li Pu with thirty thousand troops to Jinyang; Keyong sent his generals Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with troops to join them in attacking Luzhou together.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong sent Chief Commander Li Pu with thirty thousand men to Jinyang; Keyong sent Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao to join them in attacking Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏州告急於朱全忠。

translations.literal: Xia Prefecture sent an urgent appeal to Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Prefecture sent an urgent appeal to Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，全忠遣劉知俊及其將康懷英救之。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Quanzhong dispatched Liu Zhijun and his general Kang Huaiying to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Quanzhong dispatched Liu Zhijun and his general Kang Huaiying to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 楊崇本將六鎮之兵五萬，軍於美原。

translations.literal: Yang Chongben led fifty thousand troops from the six circuits and encamped at Meiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chongben led fifty thousand troops from six circuits and encamped at Meiyuan.

sentences.zh: 知俊等擊之，崇本大敗，歸於邠州。

translations.literal: Zhijun and the others struck them; Chongben was utterly defeated and returned to Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun and his forces attacked; Chongben was routed and fled back to Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 武貞節度使雷彥恭屢寇荊南，留後賀瑰閉城自守。

translations.literal: Lei Yangong, military governor of Wuzhen, repeatedly raided Jingnan; the regent He Gui shut the city and held his own.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Yangong, military governor of Wuzhen, repeatedly raided Jingnan; Regent He Gui shut the gates and held out.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠以為怯，以穎州防禦使高季昌代之，又遣駕前指揮使倪可福將兵五千戍荊南以備吳、蜀。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong considered this cowardice and replaced him with Gao Jichang, defender of Yingzhou; he also dispatched the imperial escort commander Ni Kefu with five thousand troops to garrison Jingnan against Wu and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong judged this cowardly and replaced him with Gao Jichang, defender of Yingzhou; he also sent Imperial Escort Commander Ni Kefu with five thousand men to garrison Jingnan against Wu and Shu.

sentences.zh: 朗兵引去。

translations.literal: The Lang troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Langzhou troops withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十一月，劉知俊、康懷貞乘勝攻鄜、延等五州，下之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Liu Zhijun and Kang Huaiying pressed their victory to attack the five prefectures of Bin, Yan, and others and took them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Liu Zhijun and Kang Huaiying pressed their victory, attacked five prefectures including Bin and Yan, and captured them.

sentences.zh: 加知俊同平章事，以懷貞為保義節度使。

translations.literal: Zhijun was made Associate Grand Councillor; Huaiying was made military governor of Baoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijun was appointed Associate Grand Councillor; Huaiying was made military governor of Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 西軍自是不振。

translations.literal: From this time the western armies no longer recovered their strength.
translations.idiomatic: From this point the western armies never recovered their strength.

sentences.zh: 湖州刺史高彥卒，子澧代之。

translations.literal: Gao Yan, prefect of Huzhou, died; his son Li succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yan, prefect of Huzhou, died; his son Li succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙酉，錢鏐表薦行軍司馬王景仁，詔以景仁領寧國節度使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, Qian Liu memorialized recommending the field-staff marshal Wang Jingren; an edict appointed Jingren to hold the post of military governor of Ningguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, Qian Liu memorialized recommending Field-Staff Marshal Wang Jingren; an edict appointed Jingren military governor of Ningguo.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠分步騎數萬，遣行軍司馬李周彝將之，自河陽救潞州。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong divided several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry and dispatched the field-staff marshal Li Zhouyi to lead them from Heyang to relieve Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong divided tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry and sent Field-Staff Marshal Li Zhouyi from Heyang to relieve Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏月，乙丑，廢鎮國軍興德府復為華州，隸匡國節度，割金、商州隸佑國軍。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on yichou, the Xingde Prefecture of the Zhenguo Army was abolished and restored as Hua Prefecture, subordinate to the Kuangguo military governorship; Jin and Shang prefectures were detached and placed under the Youguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on yichou, Xingde Prefecture of the Zhenguo Army was abolished and restored as Hua Prefecture under Kuangguo; Jin and Shang prefectures were transferred to the Youguo Army.

sentences.zh: 初，昭宗凶訃至潞州，昭義節度使丁會帥將士縞素流涕久之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when news of Emperor Zhaozong's violent death reached Luzhou, Ding Hui, military governor of Zhaoyi, led his officers and soldiers in white mourning garb and wept for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when news of Emperor Zhaozong's murder reached Luzhou, Ding Hui, military governor of Zhaoyi, led his officers and soldiers in white mourning and wept long.

sentences.zh: 及李嗣昭攻潞州，會舉軍降於河東。

translations.literal: When Li Sizhao attacked Luzhou, Hui led the whole army in surrender to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Sizhao attacked Luzhou, Hui surrendered his entire army to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 李克用以嗣昭為昭義留後。

translations.literal: Li Keyong made Sizhao regent of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong appointed Sizhao regent of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 會見克用，泣曰：「會非力不能守也。

translations.literal: When Hui met Keyong, he wept and said: "It is not that I lacked the strength to hold the city."
translations.idiomatic: When Hui met Keyong, he wept and said, "It is not that I lacked the strength to hold the city."

sentences.zh: 梁王陵虐唐室，會雖受其舉拔之恩，誠不忍其所為，故來歸命耳。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang bullies and abuses the house of Tang; though I received his favor in raising me up, I truly could not bear what he does—therefore I have come to submit to your command.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang tyrannizes the Tang house. Though he raised me up, I could not bear what he does—so I have come to submit to you.

sentences.zh: 」克用厚待之，位於諸將之上。

translations.literal: " Keyong treated him generously and ranked him above the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: " Keyong treated him generously and ranked him above the other generals.

sentences.zh: 己巳，朱全忠命諸軍治攻具，將攻滄州。

translations.literal: On jisi, Zhu Quanzhong ordered the armies to prepare siege equipment and was about to attack Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Zhu Quanzhong ordered his armies to prepare siege equipment for an assault on Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬申，聞潞州不守，甲戌，引兵還。

translations.literal: On renshen, he heard that Luzhou could not be held; on jiaxu, he led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he learned that Luzhou had fallen; on jiaxu he withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 先是，調河南北芻糧，水陸輸軍前，諸營山積，全忠將還，命悉焚之，煙炎數里，在舟中者鑿而沉之。

translations.literal: Earlier, fodder and grain had been levied north and south of the Yellow River and transported by land and water to the front; the camps were heaped like mountains. When Quanzhong was about to return, he ordered all of it burned—smoke and flame stretched for several li—and what was in boats was bored through and sunk.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, fodder and grain from north and south of the Yellow River had been shipped to the front until the camps were heaped like mountains. As Quanzhong prepared to withdraw, he ordered it all burned—smoke and flame stretched for miles—and supplies aboard boats were scuttled.

sentences.zh: 劉守文使遺全忠書曰：「王以百姓之故，赦僕之罪，解圍而去，王之惠也。

translations.literal: Liu Shouwen sent a letter to Quanzhong, saying: "Your Highness, for the sake of the common people, pardoned my crime and lifted the siege and departed—that was your grace."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouwen sent Quanzhong a letter saying, "Your Highness, for the people's sake, pardoned me and lifted the siege—that was a great kindness."

sentences.zh: 城中數萬口，不食數月矣。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands within the city have not eaten for many months.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands in the city have not eaten for months.

sentences.zh: 與其焚之為煙，沉之為泥，願乞其餘以救之。

translations.literal: Rather than burn it into smoke or sink it into mud, I beg the remainder to save them.
translations.idiomatic: Rather than burn it to smoke or sink it in the river, I beg you to leave what remains to save them.

sentences.zh: 」全忠為之留數囷以遺之，滄人賴以濟。

translations.literal: " Quanzhong on his account left several granaries' worth as a gift; the people of Cang relied on it to survive.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong left several granaries of supplies for them; the people of Cangzhou survived on it.

sentences.zh: 河東兵進攻澤州，不克而退。

translations.literal: Hedong troops advanced to attack Ze Prefecture, could not take it, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong troops attacked Ze Prefecture, failed to take it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 吉州刺史彭玕遣使請降於湖南，玕本赤石洞蠻酋，鍾傳用為吉州刺史。

translations.literal: Peng Gan, prefect of Ji Prefecture, sent envoys to request surrender to Hunan; Gan was originally a chieftain of the Chishi Cave barbarians, whom Zhong Chuan had employed as prefect of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Gan, prefect of Ji Prefecture, sent envoys to surrender to Hunan. Gan was originally a chieftain of the Chishi Cave people whom Zhong Chuan had appointed prefect of Ji.
